1 
 Judge Clarissa Harrell’s  
Brevard County Court Civil Division  3 
Judicial Practices and Procedures  
(Last modified November 17, 2025) 
 
 
Judicial Assistant:  Ms. Shannon Zeleniak        Shannon.Zeleniak@flcourts18.org  
       (321) 637-5305 
 Address:       The Harry T. and Harriette V. Moore Justice Center  
       2825 Judge Fran Jamieson Way  
       Viera, Florida 32940 
      
Note: Judge Harrell does not have an assigned courtroom.  Litigants should 
consult the courthouse electronic information monitor upon arrival to determine 
her courtroom assignment for a given trial or hearing. Delivery of pre-trial or 
hearing exhibit /case law binders or other hard- copy materials should be  made to 
the Second Floor Receptionist.  
Table of Contents 
A. Communications with the Judicial Office  ................................................... 2 
B. Scheduling Procedures .............................................................................. 4 
C. Remote Appearance ................................................................................... 9 
D. Submission of Orders and Judgments  ...................................................... 11 
E. Courtesy Copies of Case Law and Other Documents  ................................. 13 
F. Emergency and Other Urgent Matters  ...................................................... 14 
G. Exhibits for Evidentiary Proceedings  ........................................................ 14 
H. Pre-Trial Conferences .............................................................................. 15 
I. Forms  ...................................................................................................... 15 
J. Other Division Procedures  ....................................................................... 16 
 
  
2 
 A. Communications with the Judicial Office 
• Methods of Communication:  
• E-mail to Judicial Assistant at Shannon.Zeleniak@flcourts18.org 
is the preferred method of communication with Judge Harrell’s 
office. This optimizes clarity in communications and assists  in 
prioritizing tasks. Please note: 
• The e-mail subject line should contain the case number, 
abbreviated case name, and request (for example, “2025-CC- 
001234 – Doe v. Doe – 2-hour hearing sought”). If the message 
relates to an urgent, time-sensitive notification or request, please 
begin the subject line with the word “URGENT.” 
• Please avoid improper ex parte  e-mail communications (meaning 
messages excluding the opposing party; and see below).  Insert 
the opposing party’s e-mail address in the “cc” line of the e-mail.  
Include the e-mail address(es) that party has designated in the 
official court record  (viewable under your case number on the 
Brevard County Clerk of Court website) as well as any other e-mail address for that party known to you.   
• The JA needs to know with whom she is communicating; please 
do not blind copy any other person using the “bcc” line. 
• Please be aware that any e-mail sent to or from the judicial office may be a public record subject to disclosure.                                   
• Telephone calls can be made to the Judicial Assistant Shannon 
Zeleniak at (321) 637-5305 if necessary. 
• The Court acknowledges that although e-mail is preferred, some situations require phone calls. Notifications about an attorney or 
litigant running late or being delayed in another courtroom;  
having technology issues with Microsoft Teams sign -on; 
experiencing a car accident, medical issue, or urgent family matter; or suffering lack of access to a computer for emails, are 
all examples of situations warranting telephone calls. 
• Callers will likely first reach a Courthouse Receptionist when 
dialing the Judicial Assistant’s number. Simply state who you are 
calling for and why, your name and role in the case, the case 
number, and provide your email address and/or telephone 
number.  If the Judicial Assistant is not immediately available to 
speak to you, the Receptionist will e-mail her this information.  
3 
 The Receptionist cannot provide legal advice and may have 
limited knowledge about the Court’s procedural and scheduling 
preferences.  She often has a multitude of calls coming in for 
other judges and a line of people outside her window.  Please keep 
interactions brief and direct.  
• The judicial office does not accept text messages. 
• The Court asks all attorneys and parties to exercise the utmost cordiality and patience in telephonic communications with the 
Judicial Assistant.  Be aware that she grapples with a crush of 
inquiries over a very large caseload, sometimes with high 
numbers of urgent issues and judicial requests, every day.  
Please respect the value of her time and avoid any urge to vent or opine about people or subject matters related to your case.  She 
is a kind and compassionate person and would lend an ear if she 
were able, but she is strictly bound by ethical constraints, pressured by many demands, and may need time to consult with 
the Judge regarding scheduling or procedural questions.   
 Factual information you want the Court to know about an issue in your case should be appropriately presented in a court filing 
or at a scheduled proceeding. Realize there is nothing the Judicial 
Assistant can or should do with that information received by 
phone or e-mail. 
 It is perfectly acceptable for you to make a follow-up telephone call or send a follow-up email if your inquiry has not been 
handled within a week’s time, or sooner in the event of an 
emergency matter. 
• Ex Parte Communications:  
• All communications with the judicial office must comply with Canon 
3 of the Code of Judicial Conduct, which prohibits a judge from 
initiating, permitting, or considering ex parte communications and 
from considering other communications outside the presence of the 
parties concerning a pending or impending proceeding, unless authorized by law. All parties must be copied on any e-mail directed 
to the judicial office, unless an ex parte  communication is 
authorized by law. 
• Unsolicited Communications:  
• Parties may only contact the judicial office in accordance with these 
practices and procedures. Unsolicited communications from non-
parties will not be considered by the Court.  
4 
 • E-Filing Portal Contact Information:  
• All attorneys and self-represented litigants must make and 
receive service by e-mail, which is generally through the 
Florida Courts E-Filing Portal, unless excused. Fla. R. Gen. 
Prac. & Jud. Admin. 2.516. 
• All attorneys and self-represented litigants must provide an e-
mail address to receive signed orders electronically, unless 
excused.  Fla. R. Gen. Prac. & Jud. Admin. 2.516. It is the 
responsibility of attorneys and self-represented litigants to update their contact information using Form 2.603 any time 
there is a change in the e-mail account registered for 
electronic service. 
• Response to Inquiries: 
• The Judicial Assistant is not authorized to provide legal advice.  
Please do not ask her for it. 
• The Judicial Assistant strives to substantively respond to all 
inquiries within one business day. If she is unable to substantively 
respond within one business day, your message will be acknowledged as received with an indication of when to expect a substantive response and an alternate contact for immediate 
assistance. 
• When the Judicial Assistant is out of the office, your message will 
be acknowledged as received with an indication of when to expect a 
substantive response and an alternate contact for immediate 
assistance. 
B. Scheduling Procedures  
• Scheduling Hearings:  
• Attorneys may identify Judge Harrell’s available hearing dates and 
times utilizing the online Judicial Automated Court Scheduling 
(JACS) system, located at https://flcourts18.org/dockets-and-
calendars. Attorneys should work in good faith with the opposing 
party to try to locate mutually acceptable hearing dates and times.   
• Once agreement regarding date and time is reached, the desired time 
period may be blocked off in JACS, and a Notice of Hearing should 
be e-filed with the Clerk of Court. A copy of the e-filed Notice of 
Hearing (with Clerk’s data line appearing at top of page) must then 
be e-mailed to the JA.  Failure to e-mail the Judicial Assistant the 
5 
 e-filed Notice of Hearing within 24 hours may result in loss of the 
blocked time in JACS and require that the process start over. 
• If parties are unable to identify and mutually select a hearing date 
and time on JACS, the scheduling party should e-mail the Judicial 
Assistant, copying opposing counsel and any self-represented 
litigant, to coordinate scheduling the hearing. 
• Parties without attorneys should not use JACS. They may request 
hearing time on motions that have already been filed with the Clerk of Court by e-mailing the Judicial Assistant at Shannon.Zeleniak@flcourts18.org. It is helpful if a copy of the 
motion is attached to the e-mail with a note regarding the date it was filed, as sometimes there are processing delays with filed 
documents that prevent the Court from being able to immediately 
see them in the court record. 
• Final hearings for Uncontested Dissolution of Marriage cases are an 
exception to the above procedures. In these cases, a party seeking 
final hearing must first contact the Pro Se Coordinator at the Clerk 
of Court’s Office at prosecoordinator@brevardclerk.us or (321) 633-
7780. That Coordinator will ensure that all necessary documents 
appear in the court file before the hearing can be set. Once that has 
been accomplished, Petitioner should e-mail the Judicial Assistant 
to request a final hearing, with the option of either having a sooner final hearing conducted by a General Magistrate, or a later final 
hearing conducted by Judge Harrell. If the former is chosen, Judge 
Harrell will issue an Order Appointing General Magistrate, and once 
that Magistrate is identified, the Petitioner can schedule the hearing 
directly with that Magistrate’s office. If the latter is chosen, Judge 
Harrell will issue an Order Setting Final Hearing in her courtroom. 
• Claim of Exemption hearings in garnishment cases are also an 
exception to the above procedures. Parties file their Claims of 
Exemption with the Clerk of Court. The Clerk will schedule those 
hearings with Judge Harrell after the Clerk confirms that 
prerequisites are met. The Clerk then files a Notice of Hearing on 
Claim of Exemption in the court record and sends the Notice with hearing date and time to the parties. 
• Hearings that are improperly set or that are set contingent upon 
conditions that are not met (such as Court-mandated Registry payments in Eviction cases, for example) are subject to cancellation 
by the Court. 
• Notice of Hearing:  
6 
 • Other than as noted above, a party’s notice of hearing must be filed 
and served immediately after the reservation of hearing time. 
• A notice of hearing for a matter presumptively eligible for remote 
appearances (i.e.  other than jury trials or Order to Show Cause 
hearings) must list the Judge’s Microsoft Teams link, as follows: 
https://fl18.org/judgeharrell . 
• All notices of hearing must contain the Americans with Disabilities 
Act (ADA) notification required by Florida Rule of General  Practice 
and Judicial Administration 2.540.  
•  Matters Not Requiring a Hearing: 
□   The following matters do not need to be set for a hearing; proposed 
Orders may simply be submitted through the portal or through e-
mail to the Judicial Assistant: 
□ Stipulated Orders/Final Judgments:  The related stipulation, 
signed by both parties, should be e-filed and appear in the 
court file prior to submitting the proposed order, unless the 
signed stipulation is incorporated into the order. 
                     □ Stipulated Orders Granting Substitution or Withdrawal of 
Counsel (signed by the party/client and counsel either in 
separate e-filed motion or incorporated into the order). 
 
 •   Setting Case for Trial: 
• If a party is certain that all necessary tasks have been accomplished to prepare a case for trial, including, for example, tasks related to 
discovery, hiring of interpreters or court reporters, ascertainment of 
expert and lay witness availability, etc., the party may simply file a 
Notice for Trial and e-mail a copy of same to the JA. Be sure to indicate whether the parties are agreeing to a non-jury trial or 
whether at least one party is requesting jury trial, and include the number of trial hours or days believed to be necessary to complete 
the trial.   
• Unless the Court is already familiar with the case, it will likely then 
set a Case Management Conference so the parties can update the 
Court on all trial-related issues, and an ideal time period based upon 
the Court’s schedule availability will be established.   
• The parties are required to attend in-person mediation, telephonic 
mediation, or online dispute resolution before trial is set.  The Brevard Mediation Office can be reached at 
BrevardMediation@flcourts18.org or (321) 635-5065.  For 
information about online dispute resolution, please visit 
7 
 https://flcourts18.org/court-programs/odr. 
• Once these requirements are met, an Order Setting Trial will then 
be issued by the Court. Judge Harrell sets time-certain trials to 
provide parties with certainty and predictability. 
• Submission Deadlines:  
• Judge Harrell does not impose a deadline for pre-hearing document 
submissions, including case law, which a party may wish her to 
review in advance. She will make time to read all materials 
submitted. She asks only that the submitting party e-mail the Judicial Assistant one business day before the subject hearing to 
confirm that the previously mailed, e-mailed, or hand-delivered 
materials were actually received by the judicial office, so the JA can 
be confident that all necessary materials are in the Judge’s hands. 
Parties should remember to send opposing parties copies of 
everything they provide to the Court! 
• Please note, however, that pre-trial document submission deadlines 
cited in Orders Setting Non-Jury Trial will be enforced. 
• Order of Proceedings:  
• Matters will typically be heard in the order in which they appear on 
the docket. On occasion the Court will take up some matters ahead 
of or behind others  based upon factors like an involved attorney 
being needed in another courtroom, a participant’s need to get to a 
medical appointment, a party experiencing traffic delays, a 
necessary participant being held in custody in a courthouse holding 
cell, or a judicial preference to accommodate in-person attendees 
given the extra efforts that may have been required to appear in person. Please notify the Court via e-mail or telephone call to the 
Judicial Assistant if you have a special issue requiring adjustment 
to the order of matters being called. 
• Continuance Procedure:  
• Legally sufficient motions for continuance will be considered with 
good cause. Successive continuances absent compelling reasons are 
disfavored. Lack of due diligence is not grounds for granting a 
continuance. Except for good cause shown, the motion must be 
signed by the party requesting the continuance, as required by  
Florida Rule of General Practice and Judicial Administration 
2.545(e). 
• Motions for continuance should be filed and provided to the other 
8 
 side by the most expedient method as soon as the grounds giving 
rise to the request become known to the moving party. Ideally, this 
would be at least five business days prior to the scheduled court 
date for which the continuance is sought, barring exigent 
circumstances.  
• Motions for continuance must state with specificity: (1) the basis of 
the need for the continuance, including when the basis became 
known to the movant; (2) whether the motion is opposed; (3) the 
action and specific dates for the action that will enable the movant 
to be ready, including, but not limited to, confirming the specific 
date any required participants are available; and (4) the proposed 
date by which the case will be ready to proceed and whether that 
date is agreed by all parties. Except for good cause shown, the 
motion must be signed by the party requesting the continuance, as 
required by Florida Rule of General Practice and Judicial 
Administration 2.545(e). 
• Cancelling Hearings: 
• You may cancel hearings you have set by notifying the J udicial 
Assistant immediately. You must also immediately file and serve a 
notice of cancellation on opposing counsel and any self-represented 
litigant. 
• You may not cancel a hearing the Court has set. If the cancel lation 
is related to case settlement or resolution of the issue that was to be 
addressed at the hearing, please advise the Judicial Assistant by e-
mail and/or telephone call that this is the basis for the requested 
cancellation, and file a Notice of Settlement, with a copy of same e-
mailed to JA, as soon as possible. The Court will then issue an Order 
Cancelling Court Event. 
     Many litigants express apologetic unease regarding advising the 
Court about settlement and a need for cancellation last-minute.  
Please have no concerns about this.  Judge Harrell was a litigator 
for 30 years and is well aware that for a number of reasons, 
settlement is often not achievable until the last minutes before a 
scheduled court event. 
• You may not cancel a hearing the opposing party has set.  If there is 
a need to move it to another time, please contact the party who set the hearing and determine if it’s possible for the date to be changed, 
and for the opposing party to then file an amended notice of hearing.  
If no agreement regarding continuance can be reached, please file a 
motion to continue setting forth the detailed basis for the request 
9 
 and contact the JA for expedited hearing time on the continuance 
motion. 
C. Remote Appearance 
• Remote Appearance Procedure: 
• The Court maintains a hybrid virtual courtroom, allowing parties to 
appear either in person or remotely, as provided by Florida Rule of 
General Practice and Judicial Administration 2.530.  
• Judge Harrell encourages in-person attendance at trials and 
hearings to facilitate communication and evidence handling. 
However, absent a previously issued Order from the Court requiring 
in-person attendance, the parties, their attorneys if any, and 
witnesses may seek virtual appearance via Microsoft Teams using the following procedure:   
A. Within ten days after notice of hearing/trial is received, a party shall 
provide written notice listing those on his or her side of the case who 
intend to appear virtually, filing the notice with the Clerk and e-
mailing it to the Judicial Assistant at Shannon.Zeleniak@flcourts18.org as well as to the opposing party 
at least 14 days before the scheduled trial or hearing.  If the opposing 
party does not have an e-mail address designated in the court record, the requesting party may send the notice via regular or 
certified U.S. mail postmarked at least 14 days before trial. 
 B. If the opposing party objects to the proposed virtual appearance(s), 
he or she must file a written objection with the Clerk of Court, with a copy e-mailed to the Judicial Assistant and sent to the opposing 
party, at least five business days before hearing or trial.  The Court 
will then set an expedited hearing on the issue prior to the t rial or 
hearing date and issue an Order granting or denying the request for 
virtual appearance.  
 C. If no objection is timely filed, virtual appearances by all listed in the 
notice of intent to attend virtually shall be permitted. 
 
D. With timely notice of intent to attend virtually as set forth above, no 
motion for judicial authorization is required to be filed.  Late-filed 
notices will be scrutinized by the Court for good cause and may be 
subject to objection by the opposing party. 
 
• Platform Used:  
10 
 • The Court uses only Microsoft Teams for remote appearances. The 
only designated link for Judge Harrell’s courtroom is 
https://fl18.org/judgeharrell. (Note: this is FL as in Florida, not f1 
as in the number, then the number 18.org). No Meeting ID Number 
is required.  
• No individual invitations will be sent out to attendees using the 
Teams link. Parties can simply copy the link to either their Google 
Chrome or Microsoft Edge browser and join the virtual courtroom with Judge Harrell for the scheduled court event.   
• The Court recommends joining the Teams’ virtual lobby five to ten 
minutes before the scheduled start time.  Many scheduled hearings run longer than anticipated, so if you are not admitted right away, 
please be patient.  If it appears there will be more than a minor delay, the Court will make every effort to check in with the waiting litigants to advise them of status. 
• Requirements:  
All trials and hearings other than jury trials and Order to Show 
Cause hearings are presumptively eligible for remote appearance.  
Remote appearances at jury trials and Order to Show Cause 
hearings may still be granted on a case-by -case basis; the requesting 
party will need to file a motion and set it for expedited hearing. 
Any person appearing remotely must be in a private location that is 
quiet and free from distractions. Under no circumstances will a 
participant be permitted to appear remotely from a moving vehicle. 
Any person appearing remotely must dress and behave 
professionally in the same manner as if physically present in the 
courtroom. 
Any person appearing remotely must enable the person’s camera 
when joining the proceeding and keep the camera turned on until 
instructed otherwise by the Court. Any person appearing remotely must mute the person’s microphone 
when joining the proceeding and keep the microphone turned off 
until instructed otherwise by the Court. 
If a witness appears remotely, the party calling the witness must 
ensure the witness has a functioning camera and microphone and 
has tested the internet connection before the hearing. The oath will 
be administered in accordance with Florida Rule of General Practice 
and Judicial Administration 2.530. 
11 
 D. Submission of Orders and Judgments  
• Method of Proposed Order Submission 
• UNLESS an attorney submitting a proposed Judgment or Order is 
unable or unwilling to acquire the working knowledge of use of  
DJMCA codes required to properly electronically format a 
document to facilitate application of the Court’s electronic 
signature, submission of all proposed Judgments and Orders 
through the Court’s electronic portal is highly preferred. 
• Brevard e-portal filings require DJMCA codes on proposed 
orders.  Please refer to this announcement link for 
more information: 
http://www.brevardclerk.us/?a=Files.Serve&File_id=023197ba-
807c-4908-876a-246bd18da343 
All proposed orders must be e-filed through the Proposed Documents section of the portal in the jurisdictional map; choose Brevard 
County from the drop-down menu and select Viewer/Judicial. 
  FILING REQUIREMENTS: Each filing must contain a Cover Letter 
and at least one proposed Order. • Filer must select himself/herself in the e-service list. • COVER LETTER, PDF format • PROPOSED 
ORDER, Word document (.docx extension).  No additional formatting – text boxes, macros, headers, footers, etc.   
Use the phrase “Done and Ordered” as the last portion of the Order 
for the Judge’s signature and date codes. The Date and Signature 
codes must be on their own line and all in capital letters with all four letters in each field. The Signature code, JJJJ, must be aligned left, 
center, or right. 
There can be no characters or verbiage or use of the tab key or space 
bar before or after the codes.  
There can be attachments to the proposed order.  
The case style must reference the Eighteenth Judicial Circuit, i.e., IN 
THE COUNTY COURT OF THE EIGHTEENTH JUDICIAL CIRCUIT IN 
AND FOR BREVARD COUNTY, FLORIDA. 
Please DO NOT add the Certificate of Service codes to the proposed 
order for this division. E-Service will be provided to those selected by 
the Filer. 
12 
 • A proposed Judgment or Order can be submitted EITHER through 
the electronic portal OR via e-mail to the Judicial Assistant,  but 
NOT BOTH WAYS. Submission both ways creates potential for 
improper duplication as well as unnecessary work for the Judicial 
Assistant.   
• However, if a submitting attorney is unsuccessful in obtaining an  
electronic signature through the portal and receives consecutive “rejection/deletion” messages from the Court noting a DJMCA 
formatting problem preventing the Court’s electronic signature, 
submitting parties should not hesitate to instead send the document as an e-mail attachment to the Judicial Assistant.  That 
e-mail should contain a note that previous portal submissions 
were unsuccessful and are not being further attempted. That note 
is important to avoid the Judicial Assistant putting the Order on 
hold to ensure no further portal transmissions cause duplication.   
• The Court makes every effort to rectify formatting issues on its side 
of the portal before sending rejection messages. 
• Cover letters required to accompany portal submissions of Orders are sometimes rote, bare, and unhelpful. Judge Harrell appreciates letters that cite the date of the related hearing, if any; whether the 
proposed Order was sent to the opposing side before time of 
submission, and whether any response was received as to Order form and content; reminders of any special or unique factors or 
issues bearing on the submission previously brought to the Court’s 
attention at hearing or via court filing; where the Court might find 
necessary affidavits or other documents it may need to review in 
considering the submission (e.g. “affidavit appearing in court file 
at docket #25,” “attached to Motion for Summary Judgment at 
docket entry #11,” “attached to this letter below and e-filed on 
today’s date,” etc .). As noted elsewhere in this document, litigants 
should keep in mind that sometimes the Court is not able to see 
e-filed documents for up to five days or more, so inclusion in portal submission is beneficial. 
• When there are no attorneys involved in a case and a hearing has 
been conducted, the Judge will draft and distribute the 
appropriate Judgment or Order. 
• When a party without an attorney seeks to submit a proposed 
Judgment or Order to the Court for a matter that the submitting 
party believes does not require a hearing, that can be done either by hand delivery to the Second Floor Receptionist at The Harry T. 
and Harriette V. Moore Justice Center in Viera; via United States 
13 
 mail; or via e-mail to the Judicial Assistant, with the proposed 
Order attached, following the communication directives set forth 
in Section A, above. 
• Format: 
• All proposed orders submitted via e-mail attachment to the JA 
must be submitted in PDF format and provided to opposing counsel and any self-represented litigant. 
• All proposed orders must be accompanied by an e-mail message or cover letter either (1) certifying that all parties agree to the order or (2) containing a statement identifying any 
disagreement of the parties as to the proposed order. 
• Deadline for Submissions:  
• Absent specific directive at hearing, Judge Harrell does not 
place deadlines on attorneys for submission of proposed Orders, trusting them instead to prepare and submit the 
documents as their schedules allow.  The Court will track 
outstanding Orders and follow up with attorneys if necessary. 
E. Courtesy Copies of Case Law and Other Documents  
• Please see Sections B and D above for related topic content. 
• Unless otherwise specifically directed by the Court, it is up to attorneys and parties whether they would like the Court to consider 
any particular case law or other documents in advance of a court 
proceeding.  The Court places no deadlines for submission upon them 
but notes that if submissions are intended, professional courtesy 
recommends provision to the Court and the other side as early as 
possible to avoid delays in the proceedings, and sufficient time for the 
material to be adequately reviewed and absorbed. 
• Submission Method: 
• Courtesy copies totaling up to 30 pages may be submitted to the 
Court as e-mail attachments in an e-mail message to the JA.  The Court does not have the resources to print more than 30 pages per 
party, per case.  Submissions of 30 pages or more will need to be 
printed and either mailed or hand-delivered to the Second Floor 
Receptionist at The Harry T. and Harriette V. Moore Justice Center. 
• Self-represented litigants excused from e-mail service may submit 
14 
 courtesy copies of any number of pages to the Court by U.S. mail 
or hand-delivery to the judicial office  via the Second Floor 
Receptionist. 
F. Emergency and Other Urgent Matters  
• Requirements:  
• If a party believes there is a factual basis for setting an emergency 
hearing, a detailed motion setting forth the following must be filed: 
(1) the issues to be resolved, (2) reasons why an emergency hearing 
is necessary, and (3) the anticipated amount of time needed for each 
party’s presentation. 
• As noted above, an e -mail should be sent to the JA marked URGENT 
in the subject line, with a copy of the e -filed motion attached, and 
the opposing party copied on it. 
• Scheduling: 
• If the Court determines that an emergency exists, a hearing will 
be scheduled unilaterally by the Court. All parties shall make 
themselves available for the emergency hearing, barring exigent 
circumstances. 
G.  Exhibits for Evidentiary Proceedings  
• Submission Method and Deadlines: 
• The requirements of Section E, above, shall apply, as shall any 
specific additional directives set out in any Order Setting Trial 
issued by the Court concerning pre-trial submission deadlines and 
deadlines for party document exchange. 
• Format: 
• Ideally, all trial binders, case law and exhibits shall be submitted 
at least five days prior to the scheduled trial date. All exhibits shall be pre-marked for identification using the designations of Plaintiff’s or Defendant’s Exhibit “A” through “Z”, and if additional 
exhibits need to be marked, said exhibits shall be labeled “AA” 
through “ZZ” and so on. A copy of the exhibit list shall describe each marked exhibit.  The exhibit list shall be provided to the 
Court and the opposing party prior to the commencement of the 
trial. 
• All attorneys and self-represented litigants must bring sufficient 
15 
 copies of each exhibit for the Clerk, the Court, and each party to 
review during the hearing or trial. 
H. Pre-Trial Conferences 
• Case Management Conference (CMC):  
• Any party may request a CMC, a hearing which typically addresses 
a timeline with deadlines for various case tasks and objectives, when 
a case requires.  
• The Court strives to maintain compliance with the directives of The Florida Supreme Court in promoting effective case movement and 
management on recommended timelines, and it will sua sponte set 
CMCs when those guidelines dictate. 
• The Court strongly encourages the early use of CMCs  in more 
complex cases, multiple-party litigation, or any case that might 
benefit from court intervention.  
• Unless excused by the Court in advance, attendance at all CMCs is 
mandatory for attorneys and self-represented litigants. Parties 
represented by counsel are not required to appear at a CMC. 
• Status Conference:  
• Any party may request a status conference, as an alternate case management tool, when a case requires.   Judge Harrell finds that 
these brief hearings are effective in moving cases forward when parties or attorneys may be having a difficult time working with one 
another to advance a cause. 
• Requirements:  
• Any request for a CMC or status conference should articulate the 
reasons for the necessity of the conference. 
• Scheduling:  
• If the Court grants the request for a CMC or status conference, the 
Court will schedule the matter and issue an Order Setting Case Management or Status Hearing. Either side may move to continue the hearing if necessary due to schedule conflicts. 
I. Forms  
• Sources:  
16 
 • Parties without attorneys are encouraged to explore online and 
community resources pertaining to the drafting of notices and 
motions, substantive law, and Florida court procedures. Potential 
resources include:  
• The Florida Bar’s Lawyer Referral Service , the Brevard County 
Bar Association’s Lawyer Referral Service, and Brevard Legal Aid, each of which may be able to refer you to, or provide, free 
or reduced-cost legal consultations.   
• The Brevard County Law Library is presently undergoing 
renovations, but its  librarians are currently available in a 
Moore Justice Center kiosk to assist in providing direction 
regarding legal resources.   
• The Clerk of Court provides non-lawyer Pro Se Coordinators 
to support parties with some types of procedural and forms  
assistance, although such guidance regarding some topic 
areas of civil county court may not be available. 
• Forms may also be found at https://brevardclerk.us. 
• Parties should remain fully cognizant that anyone, any information source, who is not a Florida Bar–licensed attorney 
is not authorized to provide you with any legal advice, and 
nothing they say should be construed by you as legal advice. 
J. Other Division Procedures  
• ADA Accommodations:  
• ATTN: If you are a person with a disability who needs 
any accommodation in order to participate in this 
proceeding, you are entitled, at no cost to you, to 
the provision of certain assistance. Please contact the ADA Coordinator, Moore Justice Center, 2825 Judge Fran Jamieson Way, 3rd Floor, Viera, FL, 32940, 321- 633-2171, ext. 3, at least 7 days before 
your scheduled court appearance, or immediately on receiving this notification if the time before the scheduled appearance is less than 7 days; if you are hearing or voice impaired, call 711.  
• Interpreter Requests:  
17 
 • Information on interpreters’ services can be found on the 
Eighteenth Judicial Circuit’s website at the following link: 
https://flcourts18.org/interpreters/.  
• Please be aware that the Court does not  supply free interpreters 
for county civil matters other than Pre-Trial Conferences. It will 
be the parties’ responsibility to hire and pay necessary, qualified 
interpreters for all phases of the case. 
•  Record of Proceedings 
• Litigants should be aware that their civil case will not be digitally 
recorded, and the Eighteenth Judicial Circuit operates under an 
Administrative Order that prohibits courthouse visitors from 
recording proceedings on cellular phones or other devices. If you 
would like a record of the proceedings, a court reporter is necessary.  
To obtain a court reporter, you must contact Brevard Court Administration at (321) 633-2000 to obtain the name and telephone 
number of the official court reporter. The official court reporter will 
be able to advise you regarding the cost to secure the presence of a 
court reporter and the fees to have the record of the proceeding 
transcribed. Appeals to a higher court are governed by special rules, including the necessity of providing a complete record of the trial for 
the appellate judges to review for errors. If you choose not to arrange 
for a court reporter to attend your trial, your ability to seek appellate review of the Court’s ruling may be adversely impacted. 
 
•  Clerk of Court – Civil Division – Small Claims Pre-Trial Conferences  
 
• The e-mail address for the Clerks who primarily work with Judge  
Harrell’s division is as follows:  
VieraCivilCourtClerks@brevardclerk.us. If you have a scheduled 
Small Claims Pre-Trial Conference, please e-mail the Clerks a day in advance to obtain your case’s docket number (on that day’s list, as 
opposed to the case number), so you can report it when checking in and enable the Court to quickly locate your case when called and 
speed the overall process.

citations.quote:
Get To Know Jody Phillips
A life-long resident of Jacksonville, Jody Phillips has served as the Clerk of the Circuit Court since January 2021. Jody has over 35 years of experience in both the public and private sectors and has served in the Duval County Courthouse since 2011, where he has built long-lasting relationships with members of the public, the court system, the Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office, and all related agencies. Prior to his election as Clerk, he most recently served as the Chief Operating Officer for the Clerk’s Office, a position he had held since 2017.
During his time in office, Jody has been designated as a Certified Florida Clerk (CFC), completing hundreds of hours of specialized training covering the more than 1,000 statutory duties of the Clerk. He was re-elected to office without opposition in 2024.
As Clerk, Jody is proud to have implemented many new initiatives to assist members of the public, including a free Property Fraud Alert system, the comprehensive driver’s license reinstatement program Let’s Drive Jax!, electronically certified copies of documents, and offering expanded passport application hours.
In February 2023, Jody was elected to the CCOC Executive Council. This eight member body is elected by their fellow Clerks and sets business and budgetary policy for Clerks throughout the State of Florida.
Jody’s most cherished role is being a devoted husband to his wife Susan, and a proud father and grandfather to his two children and four grandchildren.

Clifton A. Drake
Clifton A. Drake
County: santa rosa county
Type: circuit
Divisions: Felony Division A, Felony Division B
Phone: 850-981-5632
Fax: N/A
Judicial Assistant: Cheryl Newsom, cheryl.newsom@flcourts1.gov
Address: Santa Rosa County Courthouse, 4025 Avalon Blvd. Milton FL 32583
A. Communications with the Judicial Office
Method of Communication:
All communications to the judicial office must be submitted by e-mail to cheryl.newsom@flcourts1.gov. The subject line must contain the case number, case name, and relevant matter (e.g., 25CF1234 – State v. John Doe – Hearing Requested for Motion to Suppress.)
Ex parte Communications:
All communications with the judicial office must comply with Canon 3 of the Code of Judicial Conduct, which prohibits a judge from initiating, permitting, or considering ex parte communications and from considering other communications outside the presence of the parties concerning a pending or impending proceeding, unless authorized by law. All parties must be copied on any e-mail directed to the judicial office, unless an ex parte communication is authorized by law.
Unsolicited Communications:
Parties may only contact the judicial office in accordance with these practices and procedures. Unsolicited communications from non-parties will not be considered by the Court.
E-Filing Portal Contact Information:
All attorneys and self-represented litigants must provide an e-mail address to receive signed orders electronically, unless excused.Fla. R. Gen. Prac. & Jud. Admin. 2.516. It is the responsibility of attorneys and self-represented litigants to update their contact information using Form 2.603 any time there is a change in the e-mail account registered for electronic service.
Response to Inquiries:
The judicial assistant will respond to all emails as expeditiously as possible. Please be mindful that the judicial assistant receives a large volume of communications each day. The judicial assistant is not authorized to provide legal advice.
B. Scheduling Procedures
Court Schedule:
For criminal cases, please email the judicial assistant at cheryl.newsom@flcourts1.gov for Judge Drake’s schedules for Divisions A and B.For civil cases, hearings are scheduled as needed on dates and times not reserved for criminal dockets.
Scheduling Hearings:
Hearings must be requested by contacting the judicial assistant at cheryl.newsom@flcourts1.gov. In your email, please provide the following information:
Case Number
Party Names
Attorney Names
Type of Hearing
Length requested for hearing
Any additional information (e.g. hearing needed before or after a particular date, emergency filing, etc.)
Once Ms. Newsom provides available dates, coordinate with opposing counsel to select dates that work for all parties. It is recommended that the parties agree on several potential dates in case one of the dates is no longer available by the time the hearing is confirmed. Once the parties have agreed on the potential date(s), please inform Ms. Newsom via email, and she will reply confirming that the time slot is still available and finalizing the hearing being set.
Notice of Hearing:
Once the hearing time has been confirmed, a Notice of Hearing must immediately be filed and served. The Notice of Hearing shall advise the Court and all parties of the date, time, and type of hearing. A notice of hearing involving any remote appearance must list the Judge’s Zoom credentials. All notices of hearing must contain the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) notification required by Florida Rule of General Practice and Judicial Administration 2.540.
Submission Deadlines:
Any memoranda, case law, or other documents that parties wish for the Judge to consider prior to a hearing should be emailed or e-filed at least three business days before the hearing.
Order of Proceedings:
For Expedited Docket days, Docket Days, Final Plea Days, and Violation of Probation dockets, the Court will call attorneys in the order of the sign-in sheet on the podium. Cases involving interpreters may be called prior to other matters. For Felony Miscellaneous days, a sign-in sheet will also be available, but the Court may call shorter hearings first.
Continuance Procedure:
Motions for continuance are disfavored and will be granted only upon good cause shown. Successive continuances are highly disfavored. Lack of due diligence is not grounds for granting a continuance. Except for good cause shown, the motion must be signed by the party requesting the continuance, as required by Florida Rule of General Practice and Judicial Administration 2.545(e). The motion must indicate whether opposing counsel objects to the continuance. When proposed Orders are submitted regarding Motions to Continue, the proposed Order must include the new date for which the case is being scheduled.
Cancelling Hearings:
Upon determining that a hearing is no longer necessary, please immediately notify the judicial assistant via email at cheryl.newsom@flcourts1.gov. The only way this office knows of a cancellation is through your notification. If the hearing is cancelled far enough in advance, the time can be made available to others.
C. Remote Appearance
Remote Appearance Procedure:
Requests to use communication technology for an appearance in criminal cases must be made by motion.For civil cases, most hearings will be conducted through communication technology unless otherwise requested by the parties.
Platform Used:
The Court uses Zoom for remote appearances.
Platform Meeting ID#:
860 753 2311
The following link is for Judge Drake’s Personal Meeting Room:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/8607532311
OR, parties may appear by phone by calling one of the United States Zoom telephone numbers listed below and entering Judge Drake’s PMI (860 753 2311) when prompted:
PRIMARY: (312) 626-6799
SECONDARY: (929) 205-6099
Requirements:
Any person appearing remotely must be in a private location that is quiet and free from distractions. Under no circumstances will a participant be permitted to appear remotely from a moving vehicle. Any person appearing remotely must dress and behave professionally in the same manner as if physically present in the courtroom. If a witness appears remotely, the witness must have a functioning camera and microphone. The oath will be administered in accordance with Florida Rule of General Practice and Judicial Administration 2.530.
D. Submission of Orders and Judgments
Format:
All proposed orders must be submitted in Word format and provided to opposing counsel and any self-represented litigant. All proposed orders must be accompanied by a cover letter either (1) certifying that all parties agree to the order or (2) containing a statement identifying any disagreement of the parties as to the proposed order. Proposed Orders
must
include the names
AND e-mail addresses
of all parties who need to receive e-service of the Court’s Order. Once signed by the Judge, the Order will be filed with the Clerk with e-service to the e-mail addresses provided.
Submission Method:
All proposed orders must be submitted to the Court by the proposed order portion of the Florida Courts E-Filing Portal. Please label the proposed Order being submitted with the case name and title of the Order, not just “Order.”
Deadline for Submissions:
Proposed orders must be submitted within three business days after the court proceeding.
Other Procedures Relating to Submission of Orders and Judgments:
If all parties stipulate to the Motion and/or Order (and therefore a hearing is not required), please write in the proposed Order that the parties have stipulated to entry of the Order.
Proposed Final Judgments of Foreclosure may be submitted through the e-filing portal prior to the foreclosure hearing. Judge Drake will fill in the sale date and e-file it at the conclusion of the hearing if the foreclosure is granted.
Pursuant to SRCAD2019-03, all proposed Orders in civil cases must include the following language at the end of the order, after the signature line:
In cases wherein one party is unrepresented
(pro se),
it is the responsibility of the sole attorney in the case to serve within five business days this [Order or Judgment] upon any
pro se
party who does not have access to and is not a registered user of the Florida Courts e-Filing Portal.
Please write “
DONE AND ORDERED.
” with sufficient space below for the Judge’s e-signature (five single spaced lines works best). Please do not write the date that it is done and ordered; the date will be automatically included in the e-signature. See example below:
E. Courtesy Copies of Case Law and Other Documents
When Required:
The Court does not require the submission of courtesy copies.However, courtesy copies of motions and exhibits can be helpful in civil cases.
Format:
Courtesy copies must be submitted in PDF/a format.
Submission Method:
Courtesy copies must be submitted to the Court by e-mail to cheryl.newsom@flcourts1.gov.
Deadline for Submissions:
Courtesy copies must be submitted to the Court no later than three business days before any hearing or trial.
F. Emergency and Other Urgent Matters
Requirements:
If a party believes there is a factual basis for setting an emergency hearing, a detailed motion setting forth the following must be filed: (1) the issues to be resolved, (2) reasons why an emergency hearing is necessary, and (3) the amount of time needed for each party’s presentation.
Scheduling:
Counsel must notify the judicial assistant at cheryl.newsom@flcourts1.gov regarding any emergency matters. The subject line of the e-mail must contain the word EMERGENCY.If the Court determines that an emergency exists, a hearing may be scheduled unilaterally by the Court. All parties shall make themselves available for the emergency hearing, barring exigent circumstances.
G. Exhibits for Evidentiary Proceedings
Submission Method:
Exhibits for criminal evidentiary proceedings must be presented during the hearing.However, if both the State and Defense stipulate to the Court considering certain evidence prior to the hearing (such as a forensic interview for a Child Hearsay hearing), the physical exhibit may be sent to the judicial assistant for the judge to review in chambers.In civil cases, exhibits for evidentiary hearings must be filed in the court file, and PDF courtesy copies for the Court are helpful.
Format:
Exhibits must be labeled in the following format: the State (in criminal cases) or the Plaintiff (in civil cases) shall use numbers, and the Defense shall use letters.
Deadline for Submissions:
In civil cases, electronic exhibits must be submitted three business days before the evidentiary proceeding.
H. Pretrial Procedures and Conferences
Case Management Conference:
CIVIL CASES ONLY: Any party may request a case management conference (CMC) when a case requires. The Court strongly encourages the early use of CMCs in more complex cases, multiple-party litigation, or any case that might benefit from Court intervention. Unless excused by the Court in advance, all CMCs are mandatory for attorneys and self-represented litigants. Parties represented by counsel are not required to appear at a CMC.
Status Conference:
Any party may request a status conference when a case requires.
Requirements:
Any request for a CMC or status conference must articulate the reasons for the necessity of the conference.
Scheduling:
If the Court grants the request for a CMC or status conference, the moving party must schedule the CMC or status conference pursuant to the procedures noted under the above Scheduling Procedures.
I. Setting Case for Trial
Procedure:
For criminal divisions, cases are announced as ready for trial at Docket Day, and those cases will be scheduled for Final Plea Day.If the case does not resolve at Final Plea Day, it will proceed to jury selection the following Monday.For civil cases, a Civil Pretrial and Trial Order will be entered following a Case Management Conference where the Court sets the case for trial.
Notice Period:
For criminal divisions, the Court will assign cases to specific days during the trial period at the conclusion of Final Plea Day.The Court may also assign back-up cases that must be prepared to pick juries in the event that trial days become available.For civil cases, the Court will decide which civil case(s) will proceed to jury selection no later than the Friday immediately prior to the Monday jury selection.
J. Forms
Access:
Please contact the judicial assistant at cheryl.newsom@flcourts1.gov for template orders.
K. Other Division Procedures
ADA Accommodations:
Information on ADA accommodations can be found on the circuit’s website at the following link: https://www.firstjudicialcircuit.org/public/americans-with-disabilities-act/
Interpreter Requests:
Information on interpreters’ services can be found on the circuit’s website at the following link: https://www.firstjudicialcircuit.org/public/contact-information/court-interpreter-SRC/
Three Main Rules:
Judge Drake has three main rules: Be on Time, Be Prepared, and Be Respectful. Attorneys who are delayed due to other court appearances or unforeseen circumstances should notify the judicial assistant. All attorneys are expected to have concluded any discussions with clients, victims, or witnesses prior to being in court, and criminal plea negotiations should also occur prior to coming to court. If any plea negotiations must be made the day of court, the parties should excuse themselves from the courtroom to prevent disruption of court proceedings. Everyone in the courtroom is expected to show respect for the Court and our judicial system by standing when addressing or being addressed by the Judge, not speaking when anyone else is speaking, and dressing and acting in a manner reflective of the dignified nature of court proceedings.
Decorum:
All counsel and other persons attending hearings and trials should conduct themselves in the following customary and traditional manner:
Stand as court is opened, recessed, or adjourned for all matters held in the courtroom.
Stand when the jury enters or retires from the courtroom.
Stand when addressing or being addressed by the Court for all matters held in the courtroom.
Address all remarks to the Court, not to opposing counsel.
Avoid disparaging personal remarks or acrimony toward opposing counsel and remain wholly detached from any ill feeling between the litigants or witnesses.
Refer to all persons, including witnesses, other counsel, and the parties, by their surnames and not by their first or given names.
Counsel should request permission before approaching the bench.
Unless opposing counsel has previously been shown exhibits, any exhibit offered in evidence should, at the time of such offer, be handed to opposing counsel.
In making objections, counsel should state only the legal grounds for the objection and should withhold all further comment or argument unless elaboration is requested by the Court.
Offers of, or requests for, a stipulation should be made privately, not within the hearing of the jury.
Counsel shall admonish and discourage all persons (parties, witnesses, and observers) from making gestures, facial expressions, audible comments, or the like, as manifestations of approval or disapproval during the testimony of witnesses, or at any other time.
About Us
The First Judicial Circuit is one of 20 judicial circuits in Florida. Our courts serve the people of Escambia, Okaloosa, Santa Rosa, and Walton Counties.

County Court Civil and Criminal
COUNTY COURT CIVIL
The County Civil division has jurisdiction over most landlord-tenant disputes, as well as civil matters in which the value of property, debt or other issue of controversy is between $8,001 and $50,000. These cases typically include personal injury protection and other insurance disputes; condominium and homeowner association disputes; repossession and replevin actions; and small claims cases. The County Civil Division has judges assigned at courthouses throughout Broward County, including the West Tower in downtown Fort Lauderdale, as well as regional locations in Deerfield Beach, Hollywood, and Plantation.
Video of Judge Jennifer Hilal Discussing County Civil Eviction Cases
Small claims cases involve cases over property or unpaid bills with a value up to $8,000 (excluding court costs, interest and/or attorney’s fees, if applicable). Small claims lawsuits may be filed by individuals or businesses. Special rules of procedure (
Small Claims Rules)
are designed to make the court process simpler, speedier and more informal than the regular civil court process. For info on small claims court
Click Here
.
Judge Kathleen McCarthy Discusses Small Claims
COUNTY COURT CRIMINAL DIVISION
The County Court Criminal Division handles criminal misdemeanor cases, criminal traffic matters, municipal and county ordinance violations and civil traffic infractions. Criminal misdemeanor cases include violations of the law such as Petit Theft, Simple Battery and Trespassing. Criminal Traffic matters include violations such as Driving While License Suspended, Driving under the Influence and no Valid Driver’s License cases.
Misdemeanor and Criminal Traffic matters are heard by county court judges. First degree misdemeanors are punishable by imprisonment of up to a year in the county jail and a fine of up to $1,000.00. Second degree misdemeanors are punishable by imprisonment of up to 60 days in the county jail and a fine of up to $500.00. Driving under the Influence has its own penalty provisions, which are mandated by law.
Civil Traffic infractions, which are non-criminal related violations, are generally heard by Civil Traffic Hearing Officers and consist of moving and non-moving violations. Moving violations, such as speeding and running a red light, may result in an assessment of points on your license. Other non-moving violations, such as expired registration or no seat belt, do not result in points assessed against your license.
Judge Kenneth A. Gottlieb and Judge Deborah Carpenter-Toye Discussing County Court Criminal Division
The County Court Criminal Judiciary and their staff are located at the Broward County Central Courthouse, 201 SE. 6th Street, Ft. Lauderdale, Fla. 33301 and at the three satellite courthouses located in Hollywood, Plantation
and Deerfield Beach.

County Court Civil and Criminal
COUNTY COURT CIVIL
The County Civil division has jurisdiction over most landlord-tenant disputes, as well as civil matters in which the value of property, debt or other issue of controversy is between $8,001 and $50,000. These cases typically include personal injury protection and other insurance disputes; condominium and homeowner association disputes; repossession and replevin actions; and small claims cases. The County Civil Division has judges assigned at courthouses throughout Broward County, including the West Tower in downtown Fort Lauderdale, as well as regional locations in Deerfield Beach, Hollywood, and Plantation.
Video of Judge Jennifer Hilal Discussing County Civil Eviction Cases
Small claims cases involve cases over property or unpaid bills with a value up to $8,000 (excluding court costs, interest and/or attorney’s fees, if applicable). Small claims lawsuits may be filed by individuals or businesses. Special rules of procedure (
Small Claims Rules)
are designed to make the court process simpler, speedier and more informal than the regular civil court process. For info on small claims court
Click Here
.
Judge Kathleen McCarthy Discusses Small Claims
COUNTY COURT CRIMINAL DIVISION
The County Court Criminal Division handles criminal misdemeanor cases, criminal traffic matters, municipal and county ordinance violations and civil traffic infractions. Criminal misdemeanor cases include violations of the law such as Petit Theft, Simple Battery and Trespassing. Criminal Traffic matters include violations such as Driving While License Suspended, Driving under the Influence and no Valid Driver’s License cases.
Misdemeanor and Criminal Traffic matters are heard by county court judges. First degree misdemeanors are punishable by imprisonment of up to a year in the county jail and a fine of up to $1,000.00. Second degree misdemeanors are punishable by imprisonment of up to 60 days in the county jail and a fine of up to $500.00. Driving under the Influence has its own penalty provisions, which are mandated by law.
Civil Traffic infractions, which are non-criminal related violations, are generally heard by Civil Traffic Hearing Officers and consist of moving and non-moving violations. Moving violations, such as speeding and running a red light, may result in an assessment of points on your license. Other non-moving violations, such as expired registration or no seat belt, do not result in points assessed against your license.
Judge Kenneth A. Gottlieb and Judge Deborah Carpenter-Toye Discussing County Court Criminal Division
The County Court Criminal Judiciary and their staff are located at the Broward County Central Courthouse, 201 SE. 6th Street, Ft. Lauderdale, Fla. 33301 and at the three satellite courthouses located in Hollywood, Plantation
and Deerfield Beach.

Judge Craig C. DeThomasis
The Code of Judicial Conduct governing behavior by judges forbids the judges of the Eighth Judicial Circuit to discuss pending cases with the public. Please do not call the Court expecting to speak with a Judge about any case. If you have a comment to make, please mail it to the Clerk’s Office in the appropriate county. Please keep in mind that the Court is only allowed to consider arguments made in court and documents filed by actual parties to the case. They cannot ethically read or consider any other opinions or arguments about the case, and they cannot give legal advice. Thank you.

Judge DeThomasis’ Division Procedures
Levy County Circuit Civil and Family Court
Communications with the Judicial Office
Method of Communication:
All communications to the judicial office must be submitted by e-mail to
stephensont@circuit8.org
. The subject line must contain the case number, case name, and relevant matter (e.g., 2024 DR 001234 SC – Doe v. Doe – Title of
Motion/Document
or
2-Hour Hearing Requested
.)
Ex parte Communications:
Please note that the Code of Judicial Conduct governing behavior by judges prohibits the judges of the Eighth Judicial Circuit from discussing pending cases with the public and prohibits judges from talking to any party, without all other parties present. Please do not call or email the Court expecting to speak with a Judge about any case. If you have a comment or request to make, please file it in writing with the Clerk’s Office and serve a copy on all other parties.  Please keep in mind that the Court is only allowed to consider arguments made in court and documents filed by actual parties to the case.  Judges cannot ethically read or consider any other opinions or arguments about the case, and they cannot give legal advice.
Unsolicited Communications:
Unsolicited communications from non-parties will not be considered by the court. Parties may only contact the judicial office in accordance with these practices and procedures.
E-Filing Portal Contact Information:
All attorneys and self-represented litigants must provide an e-mail address to receive signed orders electronically, unless excused. Fla. R. Gen. Prac. & Jud. Admin. 2.516. It is the responsibility of attorneys and self-represented litigants to update their contact information using Form 2.603 any time there is a change in the e-mail account registered for electronic service.
Response to Inquiries:
A judicial assistant is not authorized to provide legal advice.
Scheduling Procedures
Scheduling/Hearing Requests:
The judge’s scheduling calendars are not available online.  Hearing dates and times are provided by the JA, either by phone or by e-mail request.  When scheduling by email, the final email confirming a coordinated hearing date and time should include the case number, style of the case, the motion or motions being set, the attorneys and the amount of time being reserved.  Email communications to coordinate hearings should only be between the attorneys’ offices and should not include the judicial assistant.  Once a date has been agreed upon, an email should be sent to the judicial assistant confirming the date is still available on the Court’s calendar.  Our office does not hold suggested dates for hearings and a hearing is not scheduled on the Court’s calendar unless you receive confirmation from our office/judicial assistant.  A courtesy copy of the Notice of Hearing should be emailed to the judicial assistant.
Discovery Motions:
Florida Rule of Civil Procedure 1.380 requires the movant to provide a certificate of good faith with all discovery motions. More specifically, prior to scheduling any hearings on discovery motions, including, but not limited to, motions to compel, motions for protective orders, motions for sanctions, motions for extensions of time, etc., counsel for the moving party shall confer with counsel for the opposing party and thereafter file with the Clerk of the Court, contemporaneously with the discovery motion, a statement certifying that counsel has personally conferred with opposing counsel in a good faith effort to resolve by agreement the issues raised, without court intervention, and that counsel have been unable to do so.
If you are unable to resolve this issue after you have personally conferred, by telephone or in person
, with opposing counsel and have filed a certificate of good faith, then our office will be happy to provide you with hearing dates. Our office is unable to provide you with any hearing dates on your Motion if your Motion does not contain (or you have not filed separately) a certificate of good faith as required by the rules.
Remote Appearance
Hearings may take place entirely remotely, using telephonic or other electronic means, with no in person appearances by parties, attorneys, clerks, court reporters, or any other individuals.
Platform Used:
Our Circuit has adopted the
Zoom
platform to conduct remote hearings. Judge DeThomasis’ office is currently using this platform for remote hearings. In the case of hearings utilizing Zoom, the court will be hosting the hearing and there is no cost to any participant. You will need a computer with a web cam and microphone (preferred) or a tablet with Internet access the Zoom application. You can download the application and register for a free account at
www.zoom.com
.
Remote Appearance Procedure:
PLEASE NOTE: THE GUIDELINES BELOW ARE GENERAL GUIDELINES OFFERED TO PROVIDE THE PARTIES WITH AN OVERVIEW OF HOW A ZOOM HEARING MIGHT WORK. IN EACH INDIVIDUAL CASE, AN ORDER SETTING HEARING, WITH SPECIFIC ZOOM INSTRUCTIONS TO YOUR PARTICULAR CASE WILL BE ENTERED. IF THERE IS A CONFLICT BETWEEN THESE GUIDELINES AND THE ORDER ENTERED IN YOUR CASE, YOU SHOULD FOLLOW THE INSTRUCTIONS CONTAINED IN THE SPECIFIC ORDER ENTERED IN YOUR CASE.
Scheduling an Evidentiary Hearing:
Email the Judicial Assistant (
StephensonT@circuit8.org
) to schedule your hearing. You will need to provide the case number, subject of the hearing, amount of time requested, the names and email addresses of all attorneys and/or parties who will be participating. You may also call Judge DeThomasis’ office to schedule a hearing with all parties on the call.
Once a hearing time is scheduled, you will receive a link to a Zoom hearing. All parties should use the link to join the hearing prior to the start time. All participants shall enter their full name, when prompted. Participants may be entered into a virtual waiting room, and they will be brought into the hearing when their case is called. Due to high call volume, please expect delays and remain on the line until your case is called.
Presentation of Evidence:
If you intend to present any evidence or documents to the court at your hearing, you must pre-mark all items for identification (ex. Plaintiff’s A,B,C, etc.) and serve a copy to all parties no less than three (3) business days prior to the hearing. If there are any pro se parties involved in your case, a copy of the pre-marked evidence shall be served on them, via US Mail, no later than ten (10) days prior to the hearing.
In addition, a PAPER COPY of all pre-marked evidence, from each side, shall be received by the Court no later than the deadline contained in your specific order, typically 5 business days prior to the hearing date. This packet will be used by the Court to stamp the official evidence as it is entered at the hearing/trial.
Please confer with all parties prior to the hearing to determine whether there are any stipulations as to the admissibility of evidence. Any pre-marked evidence which is stipulated, should be so noted. All other pre-marked evidence will be considered opposed.
Appearance of Witnesses and Parties:
The attorney or party requesting that third parties attend the hearing will be responsible for sharing the Zoom hearing information with that third party and for making arrangements for their appearance. This includes witnesses, court reporters, etc. The court will not be able to call parties to include them in the hearing. The Zoom hearing information shall be provided only to third parties who are anticipated to participate in the hearing and
shall NOT be publicly published
.
Each party will need to provide the court with a list of all parties, witnesses, etc. who the party expects to participate in the Zoom hearing, no less than three (3) business days prior to the hearing. This information shall be provided via email to
StephensonT@circuit8.org
.
In some cases, you may need to email the judicial assistant (and cc the other side) with a copy of the driver’s license of each witness who you may call to testify. The driver’s license number (except the last 4 digits) may be redacted. The month and day of birth (but not the year) may also be redacted. Your order setting hearing will inform you of whether this is required in your case.
Any and all witnesses expected to testify must have video capability activated in order to be sworn.
Platform Meeting ID#:
Once a hearing time is scheduled, you will receive a link to a Zoom hearing. The Zoom hearing information shall be provided only to third parties who are anticipated to participate in the hearing and
shall NOT be publicly published
.
Decorum and Attire:
Although the hearing is being conducted virtually, proper courtroom decorum should be maintained. Participants should be in a quiet setting and minimize any external distractions. Please dress like you are coming to the courthouse.
Preparation:
Preparation and communication are keys to a successful remote hearing. Counsel and/or parties, should communicate with each other prior to the hearing and attempt to resolve as many issues as possible outside of court. Prior to the hearing date, verify your Zoom technology is operable and your connection allows for proper performance.
Submissions of Orders and Judgments
Format and Submission Method:
All proposed orders and cover letters must be submitted to the judicial assistant, through email to
StephensonT@circuit8.org
in Word format, only.  Proposed orders should NOT be filed with the Clerk of Court or filed through the e-portal.
Motions should continue to be e-filed with the Clerk’s Office.
Orders:
Unrepresented Parties/Pro-Se Parties: Proposed Orders and Judgments
Parties
not
represented by counsel and who have not consented to e-service or do not have the ability to electronically serve orders, may provide proposed orders and final judgments in paper format either by mail or hand-delivery to the Levy County Courthouse, Attn: Judge DeThomasis, 355 South Court Street, Bronson, FL 32621. The preferred method is to send proposed orders and final judgments in Word format, via email to
StephensonT@circuit8.org
.
Parties not represented by counsel can elect to receive orders from the Court by electronic mail. To elect this option, you must complete an Authorization form (available in the Clerk’s office)and file it with the Clerk of the Court.  This form of service is typically more efficient and may allow you to receive notices and orders more quickly.
If you are submitting a proposed order or judgment for the Court’s consideration and there are parties who have not consented to use of e-mail service, stamped addressed envelopes must be mailed or hand delivered to the Judicial Assistant, Teresa Stephenson.  Please clip the envelopes together, along with a sticky note that indicates the case name and case number.
Orders will not be entered until the motion has been docketed and imaged by the Clerk.
All orders or final judgments shall include a certificate of service at the bottom of the order.  Please indicate the name of the party who is to receive the order, as well as that party’s e-mail/e-service address OR mailing address, if a hard copy is required.
Attorneys: Proposed Orders and Judgments
Proposed Orders and Final Judgments are
NOT
accepted via e-filing
by the Levy County Clerk of Court.
Motions
should continue to be e-filed with the Clerk’s Office.
Proposed Orders and Final Judgments shall be
emailed to
StephensonT@circuit8.org
in Word
format
. Please do not send Proposed Orders, Motions, or supporting documentation by United States Mail. All paper filings by attorneys will be refused without processing.
The subject line in the email which submits your proposed order should provide the following:  Proposed Order/Final Judgment, [case number].
Please provide the Proposed Order or Final Judgment in Word Format, only, through email, including an enclosure letter and a courtesy copy of the Motion
.
This should be done ONLY after you have e-filed the motion and supporting documentation (if any), through the e-portal.
If you are submitting a proposed order or judgment for the Court’s consideration and there are parties who have not consented to use of e-mail service, stamped addressed envelopes must be mailed or hand delivered to the Judicial Assistant, Teresa Stephenson.  Please clip the envelopes together, along with a sticky note that indicates the case name and case number
Orders will not be entered until the motion has been docketed and imaged by the Clerk.
All orders or final judgments shall include a certificate of service at the bottom of the order.  Please indicate the name of the party who is to receive the order, as well as that party’s e-mail/e-service address OR mailing address, if a hard copy is required. The certificate of service should include the specific email address to be served and should not generally include “counsel of record”.
Emergency Orders:
If you are filing an Emergency Motion and Proposed Order, please also send an email to the Judicial Assistant immediately upon filing the motion.
Deadline for Submissions:
Proposed orders must be submitted within 30 days after any hearing, unless instructed otherwise by the Court at the hearing.
Courtesy Copies of Case Law and Other Documents
Memorandum of Law/Case Law Submissions:
Any binders containing Memorandum of Law and/or Case Law Submissions must be mailed (however NOT via email) or hand delivered to the judge’s office
at least five (5) business days
before the hearing date on your motion.
Envelopes:
Please be advised that all envelopes and postage provided by the parties become the property of the Eighth Judicial Circuit and if not used in the particular case provided, may be used in other cases.
Emergency and Other Urgent Matters
Requirements:
If a party believes there is a factual basis for setting an emergency hearing, a detailed motion setting forth the following must be filed: (1) the issues to be resolved, (2) reasons why an emergency hearing is necessary, and (3) the amount of time needed for each party’s presentation.
Scheduling:
If the Court determines that a hearing should be granted, the judicial assistant will advise the moving party of an expedited date and time for the hearing. Parties shall confirm the Court’s receipt of any “emergency” motions. If the Court determines either an “emergency” hearing is necessary or an “expedited” hearing may instead occur, in those events, it may not be possible to coordinate the date/time of such a hearing with counsel.
Emergency Motions:
A copy of any “Emergency” motion e-filed with the Clerk of Court and served upon opposing counsel should be provided to the Judge’s office for review via email to
StephensonT@circuit8.org
.
Exhibits for Evidentiary Proceedings
Format and Submission:
If you intend to present any evidence or documents to the court at your hearing, you must pre-mark all items for identification (ex. Plaintiff’s A,B,C, etc.) and serve a copy to all parties no less than three (3) business days prior to the hearing. If there are any pro se parties involved in your case, a copy of the pre-marked evidence shall be served on them, via US Mail, no later than ten (10) days prior to the hearing.
Please confer with all parties prior to the hearing to determine whether there are any stipulations as to the admissibility of evidence. Any pre-marked evidence which is stipulated, should be so noted. All other pre-marked evidence will be considered opposed.
Deadline for Submissions:
A PAPER COPY of all pre-marked evidence, from each side, shall be received by the Court no later than the deadline contained in your specific order, typically 5 business days prior to the hearing date. This packet will be used by the Court to stamp the official evidence as it is entered at the hearing/trial. If there are any pro se parties involved in your case, a copy of the pre-marked evidence shall be served on them, via US Mail, no later than ten (10) days prior to the hearing.
Pretrial Procedures and Conferences
Case Management Conference:
Requests to appear by Zoom at case management conferences should only be made after the written compliance statement has been timely e-filed as required by the Case Management Order.  The last page of the Case Management Order contains instructions for Zoom appearance.
Status Conferences/Non-Evidentiary Hearings:
Judge DeThomasis does require a written motion/order for Zoom appearance at status conferences or non-evidentiary hearings.  Any party who wishes to appear via Zoom must confirm approval to do so with his judicial assistant at least 10 days prior to the hearing, and must notify all other parties and offer to include them in a conference call to the Court.  If multiple parties will be appearing by Zoom, the party who first seeks Zoom appearance must coordinate the conference call unless otherwise agreed.  If your office prepares a notice of hearing, it must include language noting who will appear by Zoom and who will arrange the conference call, if applicable.
Parties appearing by Zoom must enter the meeting by the time of the scheduled hearing.
Judge DeThomasis will only consider written motions for a witness to appear by Zoom, if all parties consent in writing, as per Florida Rule of Judicial Administration 2.530(d)(1).
Requirements:
Any request for a CMC articulate the reasons for the necessity of the conference.
Scheduling:
If the court agrees that a CMC is required/needed, the court will enter an Order Scheduling CMC.
Forms & Equitable Distribution Spreadsheets
Division forms are available at
https://circuit8.org/self-help/forms-and-checklists/
Equitable Distribution Spreadsheet v36
Equitable Distribution Spreadsheet Instructions
Equitable Distribution Spreadsheet User Guide
Other Division Procedures
ADA Accommodations:
Under the
Americans with Disabilities Act
, if you are a person with a disability who needs any accommodation in order to participate in a proceeding, you are entitled to be provided with certain assistance at no cost to you. Please contact the ADA Coordinator, Alachua County Family and Civil Justice Center, 201 East University Avenue, Gainesville, FL 32601 (352-337-6237) at least 7 days before your scheduled court appearance, or immediately upon receiving notification of a hearing if the time before the scheduled appearance is less than 7 days. If you are hearing or voice-impaired, call 1-800-955-8770 via Florida Relay Service.
Interpreter Requests:
If an interpreter is needed for a hearing or trial, please contact
Court Interpreting
at
interpreter@circuit8.org
Levy County Guardianship
Please do not contact the Circuit Judge’s office for any Guardianship matters assigned to the General Magistrate.
For procedures, please visit our
Guardianship Procedures page
.

Probate page
for Probate Divisional Procedures, Forms and Checklist information.
