1 
 Judicial Practices and Procedures 
(Revised  July 10, 2026) 
 
Honorable George T. Paulk, Circuit Judge  
Division M 
Michelle Kolczynski, Judicial Assistant  
Contact Information 
Mailing Address: 2825 Judge Fran Ja mieson Way, Viera, Florida 32940  
Telephone: 321 -637-5644  
E-mail: michelle.kolczynski@flcourts18.org 
 
Table of Contents
 
A. Communications  with the Judicial  Office  ............................................................... 1 
B. Scheduling  Procedures  .......................................................................................... 2 
C. Remote Appearance  ............................................................................................... 6 
D. Submission  of Orders and Judgments .................................................................... 7 
E. Courtesy Copies of Case Law and Other Documents  ............................................... 9 
F. Emergency  and Other  Urgent  Matters  .................................................................... 9 
G. Exhibits  for Evidentiary  Proceedings  ...................................................................... 9 
H. Pretrial  Procedures and Conferences  .................................................................... 10  
I. Setting  Case for Trial ........................................................................................... 11 
J. Other  Division  Procedures  ................................................................................... 13  
 
A. Communications  with the Judicial Office  
 
1. Method of Communication: 
Communications to the judicial office should be submitted by e-mail to 
michelle.kolczynski@flcourts18.org and the subject line must contain the case 
number, case name, and relevant  matter (e.g., 2024-CF-001234-A– State of 
Florida v. Doe). 
 
2. Ex parte Communications:  
All communications with the judicial office must comply with Canon 3 of 
the Code of Judicial Conduct, which prohibits a judge from initiating, permitting, or considering ex parte communications and from considering 
other communications outside the presence of both or all the parties  
concerning a pending or impending proceeding, unless authorized by law.  
 
  This Court CANNOT AND WILL NOT accept any ex-parte communications      
 or correspondence in any case. All parties must be copied on any e-mail      directed to the judicial office, unless an ex-parte communication is   
 authorized by law.  
 
2 
  
If a matter needs to be brought to the Court’s attention, a proper motion must 
be filed with the Clerk of Court and served on all parties and/or counsel. 
Arguments and negotiations between the parties should remain between the 
parties, and the Court should not be included in such communications. 
 
3. Unsolicited Communications:  
Unsolicited communications from non-parties will not be considered by the 
court. Parties may only contact the judicial office in accordance with these 
practices and procedures. 
 
4. E-Filing Portal Contact Information:  
All attorneys and self-represented litigants must provide an e-mail address 
to receive signed orders electronically, unless excused. Fla. R. Gen. Prac. & 
Jud. Admin. 2.516. It is the responsibility of attorneys and self-represented 
litigants to update their contact information using Form 2.603 any time 
there is a change in the e-mail account registered for electronic service.  
 
5. Response to Inquiries:   
The Judicial Assistant is not authorized to provide legal advice. If the 
Judicial Assistant is out of the office, an email will be provided for 
emergencies only. 
 
B. Scheduling Procedures  
 
1.  Meet and Confer Requirement:  Pursuant to Rule 1.202 before filing a non-dispositive motion, the moving 
party is required to confer (in person or by telephone/video conference) with 
the opposing party in a good-faith effort to resolve the issues raised in the 
motion.   It shall be the responsibility of the attorney who schedules the hearing to 
arrange the conference. Opposing Counsel must respond promptly to inquiries and communications. 
At the end of the motion, above the signature block the moving party must 
include a certificate of conferral indicating the Parties have complied with the 
Rule, prior to filing the motion. The Certificate of Conferral shall be indicated 
in the following form:   
“I certify that prior to filing this motion, I discussed the relief requested i n this 
motion by [method of communication and date] with the opposing party and the 
[opposing party ( agrees or disagrees) on the resolution of all or part of the 
motion].”  
 
OR  
 
“The opposing party did not respond (describing with particularity all of the 
3 
 efforts undertaken to accomplish dialogue with the opposing party prior to filing 
the motion).”  
 
OR 
 
“I certify that conferral prior to filing is not required under rule 1.202.” (Please     
see rule 1.202(c) for exemptions)  
 
2. Scheduling Hearings:  
 
Meet and Confer:  
The Court has a mandatory meet and confer policy before scheduling    
hearings. Hearing cannot be scheduled until after the Meet and Confer has    
taken place.  
 
Coordination between the Parties:  All hearings must be coordinated with all parties (including pro se) before 
scheduling. The parties shall comply with the Guidelines for Professional 
Conduct applicable to Scheduling, Continuances and Extensions of Time as 
set forth in the 2022-2024 Professionalism Handbook published by the Florida Bar.  If there are difficulties coordinating a hearing with the opposing 
party/counsel, the scheduling party should schedule a 5-minute, short-matter hearing to discuss this with Judge Paulk.  
 
Scheduling Platform – JACS (Judicial Automated Calendaring System). Hearings must be scheduled using the court’s online scheduling platform, 
JACS (Judicial Automatic Calendaring System). If more than fifteen (15) 
minutes is needed, please reserve additional time slot(s) until the desired amount of time is reserved. (e.g., 1 hour is needed, select four consecutive 
time slots).  
 
PRO SE (party without an attorney) Scheduling Procedures: A pro se party can view available hearing time in JACS at the following  link: https://jacs.flcourts18.org/public-court/20.  
 
Once the pro se party has coordinated availability with the opposing  
counsel/party and are ready to schedule a hearing, they must email the  
Judicial Assistant at michelle.kolczynski@flcourts18.org to have the court  
reserve the agreed-upon hearing time.  
 
 Scheduling Procedures for Attorneys:  All hearings are scheduled through the JACS (Judicial Automated 
Calendaring System), which is accessible through the Court’s website, the 
Eighteenth Judicial Circuit Courts at https://flcourts18.org or directly 
through the JACS login at https://jacs.flcourts18.org/login. A JACS account 
(only available to attorneys), is required. 
 
 
 
4 
 Short Matter Hearings:  
5-minute hearing time is available for uncontested matters only, that can        
 be heard by the Court in 5-minutes or less. These timeslots may not be  
combined. If additional time is needed, seek additional hearing time.  
       Short Matter hearing time is generally 8:30 a.m. – 9:00 a.m., Tuesday         through Friday except on Pre-Trial Conference and Trial days. Short matter  
hearings will only be conducted remotely via Microsoft Teams (“Teams”). 
  
Hearings less than 2 hours:  
Hearing time is available in 15-minute increments. If additional time is 
needed, please reserve additional time slot(s) until the desired amount of time 
is reserved. (e.g., 1 hour is needed, select four consecutive time slots).  
 
 All non-evidentiary hearings, less than two hours are conducted remotely via  
 Microsoft Teams.  
 
Email confirmations sent by JACS are not to be used in place of Notice of 
Hearings and Notice of Cancellations.  
 
Hearings of two to four hours: 
Hearing time over two hours must be approved by the Judicial Assistant. 
Please send an email request, with details to  michelle.kolczynski@flcourts18.org. 
 
     Non-evidentiary hearings of two hours or more hours may be conducted remotely, via Teams, or in person if all parties agree. The Judicial Assistant 
should be notified in advance of any in-person hearings of two hours or more 
so a courtroom can be requested to accommodate all parties. At least two 
weeks’ notice is requested.  
 
Cross Noticing Hearings: Any requests to cross-notice a hearing should first 
be directed to the party who scheduled the hearing. If the parties agree, please 
then contact the Judicial Assistant for approval. 
 
Motions for Attorney’s Fees and Costs : Unless otherwise agreed, the Court 
will first hear arguments and determine the movant’s entitlement to fees 
before scheduling a hearing to resolve any disputes regarding the amount of fees or costs. Any hearing must be coordinated through the Judicial 
Assistant. To expedite resolution of the issues, the Court may enter an Order providing the parties with specific directives and timelines. 
 
3. Matters not requiring a hearing:  Most agreed/stipulated matters 
Motion for Substitution of Counsel Motion to Withdraw (with written client consent) 
Plaintiff’s Motion to Reschedule Foreclosure Sale Date 
Appointment of Attorney Ad Litem   
 
5 
 4. Notice of Hearing: A Notice of Hearing must be filed within 24 hours and 
served immediately after reserving hearing time. All notices of hearing must 
contain the ADA notification required by Florida Rule of General Practice and 
Judicial Administration 2.540. 
Requirements: The Notice of Hearing must contain the following:  
 
• The date and time of the hearing.  
• The amount of time reserved for the hearing.  
• The name of the Motion(s) to be heard; The date of filing of the Motion(s); The Clerk’s Docket Number of the filed Motion(s) [not the e-Portal filing number].      
   
   
  
• The location of the hearing – The address of the Moore Justice Center 
(2825 Judge Fran Jamieson Way, Viera, FL 32940) for all in -person 
hearings. The Notice must state “Via Microsoft Teams” instead of the 
Courthouse address for all remote hearings and include the 
highlighted below (note: the Court will not be providing a link at a 
later time):  
Platform Meeting ID#: https://fl18.org/gpaulk 
Meeting ID: 217 653 736 381 
Passcode: kx3DR9rD 
 
TEAMS Audio only: 1-386-310-1754 Phone Conference ID : 809 728 185# 
 
• Certificate of compliance with Meet and Confer requirements [see 
Section B.1 supra ]. 
• ALL NOTICES OF COURT PROCEEDINGS MUST INCLUDE THE UPDATED ADA STATEMENT (EFFECTIVE July 1, 2026) as outlined in 
Brevard County ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER NO. 26-27, signed  June 
30, 2026) and pursuant to Rule 2.540(c), Fla. R. Gen. Prac. & Jud. 
Admin.  Specific language may be found on the court’s website at 
https://flcourts18.org/americans-with-disability-act-compliance/and 
in section J of these procedures.  
• Requirements for Notice of Evidentiary Hearing:  If the hearing is an evidentiary hearing, the Notice must be titled as such: “Notice of 
Evidentiary Hearing.” 

6 
 5. Hearing Submissions and Deadlines:  Printed Copies of all Notice of 
Hearings, Motions, Reponses, etc., are required to be sent to the judicial office 
and must be received no later than 2 weeks prior to the scheduled hearing. 
The judicial office will not be printing hearing documents. Documents not 
received by this deadline may result in the cancellation of the hearing, without 
notice to the scheduling party.  
Motions/pleadings over twenty pages must be placed in a binder with an    
index page and tabbed. Do not staple.  
6. Order of Proceedings: Matters will be heard in the order they appear on        
the docket. If the prior hearing runs later than scheduled, patience is 
requested. The next matter will be called up when the prior hearing 
concludes.  
7. Cancellation Procedures: A Notice of Cancellation must be filed and is 
required to cancel a hearing. The filing of the Notice of Cancellation is not 
sufficient notice of cancellation. The notice should be emailed to the Judicial 
Assistant at michelle.kolczynski@flcourts18.org and all parties notified of the 
cancellation as soon as possible.  The Court must confirm the cancellation. It 
is also the responsibility of the scheduling party to cancel the hearing in JACS. Do not assume that the hearing is automatically removed from the 
Court’s calendar. If you are unable to cancel the hearing in JACS, please 
notify the Judicial Assistant.  
C. Remote Ap pearance  
 
  Remote Appearance Procedure: The court prefers remote appearance as  
      outlined in section 2, but maintains a hybrid virtual courtroom, allowing    
      parties to appear either in person or remotely, as provided by Florida Rule of  
      General Practice and Judicial Administration 2.530 
 
  Platform Used: The Court uses Microsoft TEAMS for remote appearances. 
  Please be sure to have tested your TEAMS connection prior to the scheduled        
  event. You will be looking for the lobby entitled: “JUDGE PAULK NEW 
VIRTUAL COURTROOM” (found in the upper left-hand corner of your screen).  
  
Platform Meeting ID#: https://fl18.org/gpaulk  
Meeting ID: 217 653 736 381 
Passcode: kx3DR9rD  
 
TEAMS Audio only: 1-386-310-1754 
Phone Conference ID : 809 728 185# 
 
Please note that Judge Paulk utilizes the same TEAMS link for all court  events. Judge Paulk will admit all parties as soon as possible following the  
conclusion of the proceeding scheduled prior to yours. Your patience is  
greatly appreciated. 
7 
 Requirements:  
 
• Any person appearing remotely must be in a private location that is   
quiet and free from distractions. Under no circumstances will a 
participant be permitted to appear remotely from a moving vehicle. 
 
• Any person appearing remotely must dress and behave professionally        
in the same manner as if physically present in the courtroom. 
 
• Any person appearing remotely must enable the person’s camera when joining the proceeding and keep the camera turned on until instructed otherwise by the court. 
 
• If a witness appears remotely, the party calling the witness must  ensure the witness has a functioning camera and microphone and has tested the internet connection before the hearing. The oath will be administered in accordance with Florida Rule of General Practice 
and Judicial Administration 2.530. 
 
Technology Needs: Microsoft TEAMS. Microsoft TEAMS works best when the 
application is downloaded but it is not necessary to do so.   
      
D. Submission  of Orders  and Judgments  
 
IMPORTANT NOTE: effective 09/02/2026 the FORECLOSURE SALE 
LOCATION  for Brevard County has changed.  Foreclosure auctions prior 
to 09/02/2026 are held at 11:00 a.m. at the North Brevard Government 
Center, Brevard Room, 518 S. Palm Ave., Titusville, Florida.  Foreclosure 
auctions on or after 09/02/2026 are held online at https://www.brevard.realforeclose.com.  Please be sure to make the 
appropriate changes to your proposed Orders and Summary Judgments.   
 
 Cover Letter: All proposed orders must be accompanied by a cover letter 
indicating (1) the subject, and the date and time heard, (2) indicate that all 
parties have been provided with the same materials and (3) certifying that all 
parties agree to the order or a statement identifying any disagreement of the 
parties as to the proposed order.   
Deadline for Submissions: Unless otherwise specified, all proposed orders  
must be submitted within 10 days after any hearing.   
Format : 
 
Proposed Orders When the Court Makes a Ruling: The introductory 
paragraph of the Order must include the date of the hearing and the title.  
All orders must describe the subject and ruling of the Court.  
8 
  
If the parties disagree, both parties should submit a proposed order as 
outlined below.   
Proposed Orders Without a Hearing: All "Consent" or "Agreed" Orders shall 
include the word "Consent," "Agreed," or “Uncontested” in the title of the 
proposed Order, and must include in the title the subject and ruling of the 
Court. The introductory paragraph of the proposed Agreed Order must include 
the title, date filed, and Clerk’s docket number of the subject Motion, and must 
state that the matter came before the Court upon the agreement of the parties. 
 
All Orders must contain the following statement: 
It is further ADJUDGED that within five days from the date of eservice of this Order, the Petitioner shall: Furnish a copy of this Order to each self-represented party by U.S.
 Mail, first 
class, postage paid; and File a certificate signed by 
Petitioner's counsel that delivery of this Order has been 
made as set forth herein. 
 
Submission Method: Agreed orders, should be submitted through the 
“proposed order” section of the Florida Courts E-Filing Portal.   
Portal submissions are required to be formatted with the “DJMCA” codes. The 
DJMCA codes identify where to place electronic signatures, dates, and related 
information.   
• DDDD is the code used for the date the Judge signs the Order; JJJJ is the 
code for the Judge's signature. For the Certificate of Service, MMMM is the 
code for the mailing/service date; CCCC is the code for the service list, and 
AAAA is the code for the Judicial Assistant's signature. 
 
• The signature code (JJJJ and AAAA) must be on its own line. It can be left, center, or right justified. It cannot be "fully" justified. There can be no 
characters, spaces, or tabs before or after the signature code.  The proposed 
order submission shall include the proposed order itself, which must be a Microsoft Word document, in the .docx format, with 1” margins, with no 
unnecessary formatting (i.e., do not include text boxes, macros, headers, 
footers, etc.); and a cover letter, which must be submitted in .pdf format. 
 
Orders that are Not Agreed to: If the parties are unable to agree on the form 
of the order that accurately reflects the Court’s ruling, both sides shall 
present their respective proposed orders to the court for consideration within 
seven (7) days of the hearing, via email with copies to opposing counsel. 
 
• The party objecting to the proposed order shall also present a “redline”  
version of the proposed order to the Court, in Microsoft Word format and using the “Track Changes” function, together with a transcript of the 
holding if a Court Reporter was requested by any party. 
9 
  
• The purpose of providing the Court with a “redline” version of the proposed 
order in Microsoft Word format, using the “Track Changes” function, is to allow the Court to compare the versions of the competing proposed orders 
to consider and comprehend what has been changed, revised, or added. 
Copies of any such “redline” version of the proposed order and hearing transcript shall be provided to opposing counsel/ unrepresented party. 
 
Foreclosure packets must be submitted by mail, courier, or by delivery 
agency with a signature block for hand signature, and include copies for 
conforming and addressing, postage paid/affixed envelopes. PLEASE NOTE 
THE FORECLOSURE SALE LOCATION CHANGE EFFECTIVE 09/02/2026 
(See Section D).  
 
E. Courtesy  Copies of Pleadings, Case Law, and Other Documents  
 
Courtesy copies of pleadings, case law, and other documents: printed 
copies are required and must be submitted to the court for any hearing at 
least 2 weeks prior to the hearing. 
Submission Method: Motions/pleadings over twenty pages must be printed in 
paper format (unless directed otherwise), placed and submitted in a binder with 
an index page and tabbed and should be submitted by mail, courier, hand 
delivery, delivery carrier (UPS, FedEx, etc.) Deadline for Submissions: No later than 2 weeks, prior to the court event. 
F. Emergency  and Other  Urgent  Matters  
 
Requirements: If a party believes there is a factual basis for setting an  
emergency hearing, a detailed motion setting forth the following must be  
filed: (1) the issues to be resolved, (2) reasons why an emergency hearing is  necessary, and (3) the amount of time needed for each party’s presentation. 
 
The Motion should be provided to the Court for review and will be accepted 
by email.  
 
Scheduling: If the court determines that an emergency exists, a hearing  will be coordinated by the parties or may be scheduled unilaterally by the 
court. All parties shall make themselves available for the emergency hearing,  
barring exigent circumstances. 
G. Exhibits  for Evidentiary  Proceedings  
Submission Method:  
Remote Proceedings: Paper exhibits, pre-marked for identification in the 
format described below, together with an exhibit log must be delivered to 
10 
 chambers, at least three business days in advance of the hearing or trial. 
In-Person Proceedings: On the day of the hearing or trial, please bring 
sufficient copies of the pre-marked exhibits for the Judge and opposing 
counsel or party, together with an exhibit log. 
Format: The court clerks label the evidence with the proper evidence stickers 
during trials only. Attorneys must pre-mark the evidence for identification 
purposes and provide the clerk with an exhibit log notating the description of 
the evidence along with the referenced identification. Identifications should 
be marked as letters, starting with A, B, C, D, … etc. Should the exhibits 
exceed Z, they will need to be marked as AA, AB, AC, AD, … etc. The mark 
may be placed anywhere on the exhibit, provided it is easily visible.  Exhibits may 
be in folders, binders, boxes, or whatever makes them easy to locate and 
organize. 
Deadline for Submissions: Exhibits for remote evidentiary proceedings must  
be received in chambers three business days before the evidentiary 
proceeding. 
H. Pretrial  Procedures  and Conferences  
Case Management Conference (CMC): Any party may request a case 
management conference (CMC) when a case requires. The court strongly 
encourages the early use of CMC in more complex cases, multiple-party 
litigation, or any case that might benefit from court intervention. Unless excused by the court in advance, all CMCs are mandatory for attorneys and 
self-represented litigants. Parties represented by counsel are not required to 
appear at a CMC. 
Status Conference: Any party may request a status conference when a case 
requires. 
Requirements: Any request/motion for a CMC or status conference must 
articulate the reasons for the necessity of the conference.  
Scheduling: A CMC may be scheduled through the JACS platform as you would 
any other hearing. If suitable hearing time cannot be found in JACS, send an 
email request to the Judicial Assistant at michelle.kolczynski@flcourts18.org  
listing the matters to be addressed at the CMC and the amount of hearing time requested, so that the court can assist with scheduling.  
 
Pretrial Procedures and Pre-Trial Conferences (PTC): Printed, courtesy 
copies of Pretrial Stipulations, Jury Instructions and Verdict Forms must be submitted to the judicial office no later than three days prior to the Pretrial Conference for the Court’s review for Pretrial Conference. DO NOT EMAIL.  
 
No motions will be heard at the Pre- Trial Conference . 
 
11 
 In-person appearance is required at pre-trial conferences in jury trial cases, 
unless otherwise indicated or previously excused. After appearing in person at 
the initial pre-trial conference, the parties may appear at subsequent pre-trial 
conferences remotely via TEAMS. 
 Non-jury trial pre-trial conferences and foreclosure pre-trial conferences are 
conducted remotely via TEAMS. 
 
I. Setting  Case for Trial 
 
 Trial dates for each civil division are available on the Eighteenth    
Judicial Circuit’s website at: https://flcourts18.org/dockets -and-calendars/  
 
For assistance regarding Civil Case Management Orders or Trial-related 
questions, please contact the Civil Case Manager, Joanna Linkous, at either of 
the following:  
321-633-2128 
Joanna.Linkous@flcourts18.org 
 
For assistance regarding Foreclosure Civil Case Management Orders or Trial 
related questions, please contact the Foreclosure Civil Case Manager, Cayla 
Duffy, at either of the following:  
321-264-7720 
Cayla.duffy@flcourts18.org 
 
 
Administrative Order No. 25-08 (effective February 1, 2025): Counsel is 
expected to comply with Administrative Order No. 25-08, concerning Civil Case Management. For all applicable Circuit Civil cases filed in this Circuit after 
February 1, 2025, the Plaintiff must make an initial designation of Case 
Management Track on the Civil Case Management Track Designation Form, 
(attached to AO 25-08 as “Exhibit. A”).  
 
The Plaintiff is required to file the Civil Case Management Track Designation 
Form at the time of the initial filing of the action along with the Complaint, 
Summons and Civil Cover Sheet. Unless the Plaintiff files a completed Civil 
Case Management Track Designation Form at the time of the initial filing of the 
action, the Clerk will reject the initial filing which will be placed in the 
correction queue for a period of thirty (30) days. If the Plaintiff files the 
completed Civil Case Management Track Designation Form  within the thirty 
(30) day period, the Clerk will accept the filing, and the action will commence as of the date of the initial filing. If the Plaintiff fails to correct this within 
the time allotted, the action will not commence, and the Plaintiff will have 
to refile the action. 
Upon the commencement of the action and based on the specified track 
indicated in the Civil Case Management Track Designation Form, the Court will 
issue the uniform Case Management Order for the Streamlined Track or 
12 
 General Track. Cases designated as Complex on the Civil Case Management 
Track Designation Form will be issued a General Case Management Order 
which will control the case until a proper motion to designate the case as 
Complex (Rule 1.201) is filed and heard. 
Actual Trial Period and Pre-Trial Compliance Orders: A Trial Order will be 
issued 120 days prior to the Projected Trial Period specified in the Case 
Management Order. The Trial Order will set the Actual Trial Period, the Pre-
Trial Conference date, and Direct Pre-Trial Compliance to be completed prior 
to the Pre-Trial Conference. Failure of the pleadings to be closed will not 
preclude the court from setting a case on an Actual Trial Period. 
 
Amendment of Case Management Order/Trial Continuances. Deadlines in 
the Case Management Order must be strictly enforced unless changed by court order.  
Prior to issuance of an Actual Trial Period. Parties may submit an agreed 
order to extend a deadline if the extension does not affect the ability to comply 
with the remaining deadlines or the Projected Trial Period in the Case 
Management Order. If an extension affects a subsequent deadline or the 
Projected Trial Period, the Parties may seek amendment of the Case Management Order pursuant to Fla.R.Civ.P. 1.200(e)(3).  
After an Actual Trial Period has been set by the Court; if an extension will 
affect a subsequent deadline (but not the Actual Trial Period) the Parties may 
seek amendment of the Case Management Order pursuant to Fla.R.Civ.P. 
1.200(e)(3)   
If an extension affects the Actual Trial Period, the Parties must seek a 
continuance of the Actual Trial Period pursuant to Fla.R.Civ.P. 1.460. Continuances of Projected and Actual Trial Date: Continuances are 
disfavored and will be granted only upon good cause shown. If the case has not 
yet been set for trial, a Motion to Continue must comply with the requirements of Rule 1.200(e)(3) of the Florida Rules of Civil Procedure. If an Order Setting 
Trial has been entered into the case, a Motion to Continue must comply with 
Rule 1.460.  Except for good cause shown, the motion must be signed by the 
party requesting the continuance, as required by Florida Rule of General 
Practice and Judicial Administration 2.545(e).  
If the parties agree on a trial continuance, a proposed order may be submitted 
for consideration by the Court. The order must contain a new trial and pre-trial 
conference date, and discovery must be addressed. Without these items, the 
order will not be considered and must be scheduled for hearing. If a hearing is 
required, the filing party will be notified. If the parties disagree, a hearing must 
be scheduled.  
 Rule 1.440 Setting Action for Trial: If a party seeks a trial before the 
projected or actual trial date, any party may file a Motion to set the matter for 
13 
 trial and must serve a copy of the motion on the presiding judge. 
 
Trial Dates During the Trial Period: The court does not set date-certain 
trials. After the pre-trial conference, the court will issue its Order of Trials. The 
numerical order of cases will be followed as closely as possible, but to  
maximize the use of the trial days, the court may call cases up for trial out of 
sequence. Attorneys, self-represented litigants, parties, and witnesses are 
expected to be ready for trial within twenty-four (24) hours.   Rollover Cases: Any case that is scheduled but not heard during the trial 
period will be rolled to the next scheduled trial docket. However, Judge Paulk prefers that the parties confer and mutually agree upon a future trial date to 
allow for adequate planning and preparation by all parties. Once a trial docket 
has been agreed upon, please notify the Judicial Assistant and the Civil Case Manager.  
 
Trial Settlement: The Civil Case Manager and the Judicial Assistant should 
be notified of any settlement affecting an upcoming trial docket as soon as practicable. To be released from the pre- trial conference and/or trial docket, 
at a minimum, a Notice of Settlement must be filed and provided to the Court.  
 All parties must at all times comply with the “Courtroom Decorum Rules” 
which can be found on the Eighteenth Judicial Circuit Court’s website at 
https://flcourts18.org/courtroom-decorum/ 
 
J.  Other  Division  Procedures  
 
• Required ADA Statement all notices of court proceedings, whether an order issued by a judge or a notice filed by an attorney or party, and all process compelling appearance, including but not limited to a summons, 
at court proceedings must include the following statement in bold face, 14-
point Bookman Old Style or Arial font:  
 
If you are a person with a disability who needs any 
accommodation in order to participate in this proceeding, you are entitled, at no cost to you, to the provision of certain assistance. Please contact [ADA Coordinator, applicable address, and applicable t elephone number] at least 7 days 
before your scheduled court appearance, or immediately on receiving this notification if the time before the scheduled appearance is less than 7 days; if you are hearing or voice impaired, call 711.  
 
• Court Reporters are not provided by the Court. The use of a court 
reporter is solely the responsibility of the party or parties.  
• Courtroom Decorum: All parties must at all times comply with the 
14 
 “Courtroom Decorum Rules” which can be found on the Eighteenth 
Judicial Circuit Court’s website at https://flcourts18.org/courtroom-
decorum/ 
 
• Courtroom Technology:  Information regarding available courtroom equipment, technology, or to make a reservation for a specific item, may be accessed on the Eighteenth Judicial Circuit Court’s website at 
https://flcourts18.org/courtroom-equipment/ 
 
• Interpreter Requests: If an interpreter is needed for a hearing or trial, 
please contact Court Administration at 321-633-2171.

﻿GINGER LERNER-WREN
COUNTY COURT JUDGE
COUNTY COURT CRIMINAL
SEVENTEENTH JUDICIAL CIRCUIT 
                  Courtroom 6155 
    Judicial Assistant, JoAnne Iovino 
	  

	

BROWARD COUNTY COURTHOUSE
201 S.E. 6th Street 
Fort Lauderdale, FL  33301
(954) 831-7240
                        Fax  (954) 831-6533
                jwren@17th.flcourts.org






	







On behalf of County Court Judge Ginger Lerner-Wren


Welcome to Divisions MS and Division MI - Broward’s Mental Health Court.


As Per the Florida Supreme Court Workgroup Mandate






The Following Division Practice & Procedures Shall be Discussed:




1. Remote Appearance (availability, procedures)          Pg. 2


2. Hearing Procedures (Scheduling, noticing,               Pg. 2-3
          Continuance, cancellation) 


3. Communication with Judge’s Office                           Pg. 5


4. Submission of Orders                                                   Pg. 6


5. Courtesy Copies (to chambers, opposing parties)    Pg. 6


6. Emergency and Other Urgent Matters                         Pg. 6


7. Exhibits for Evidentiary Proceedings                          Pg. 7


8. Pretrial Procedures and Conferences                         Pg. 7 


9. Setting Case for Trial                                                    Pg. 7


10. Preferred Division Forms                                             Pg. 7
                             
11. (Other Division Procedures)                                        Pg. 7 








REMOTE APPEARANCE 


In an effort to promote access to court process, remote appearances via ZOOM are permitted for both the MS Division and Mental Health Court, for the following procedures: 


1. Arraignments, 




2. Court Status Hearings, and 




3. Calendar Call Dockets


4. All other remote hearing requests must be in writing via email to Judicial Assistant, JoAnne Iovino, jiovino@17th.flcourts.org 






DIVISION MS & MI (MENTAL HEALTH) SCHEDULING 




MONDAY


8:30am    MI In-Custody Hearings 


9:30am    Calendar Call, Status Hearings, Change of Pleas, Motions To 
                 Compel 


1:30pm    1st Violation of Probation Hearings 


2:00pm     Evidentiary Motions (i.e., Motions to Suppress, Motion to Dismiss, Stand Your Ground Motions, Non-Jury Trial, Restitution. 




TUESDAY


8:30AM   Division MS Arraignments 


9:30AM   Jury Trials 




Wednesday 


8:30AM MI (Mental Health) In-custody hearings & MS Arraignments, VOP’s 


9:30AM     Calendar Calls, Change of Pleas, Motion to Compel, Pleas Conf. 


10:30AM    Continuation of Jury Trials 




THURSDAY


8:30am MI (Mental Health) In-custody hearings & MS Arraignments, VOP’s 


9:30AM Calendar Calls, Change of Pleas, Motion to Compel, Plea Conf. 


1:30pm   Mental Health Court Docket 




FRIDAY


8:30am MI (Mental Health) In-custody hearings & MS Arraignments, VOP’s 


9:30AM Calendar Calls, Change of Pleas, Motion to Compel, Plea Conf. 


1:30pm     Evidentiary Motions (i.e., Motions to Suppress, Motion to Dismiss, Stand Your Ground Motions, Non-Jury Trial, Restitution, etc.)  






HEARING PROCEDURES 


Judge Lerner Wren’s courtroom is located in the West Wing of the Central Courthouse, located at 201 Southeast 6th Street, Fort Lauderdale, FL. 33301
The courtroom is located on the 6th floor, west wing, Courtroom 6155. 


LINK TO ZOOM: https://17thflcourts.zoom.us/j/500897463


ZOOM MEETING ID: 500 897 463


The following rules apply to all in-person court attendees: 


1. No beverages are permitted in the courtroom


2. No children under the age of 13 years old. 


3. Cellphones must be on silent and no video recording is permitted. 


4. Appropriate attire is required for both in-court and remote hearings. 


5. If on ZOOM, all court attendees must identify themselves by their last name.


6. Court decorum is essential for all Zoom court hearings. For example, all ZOOM Court participants shall ensure they are in appropriate settings where it is quiet, and no driving shall be permitted. 


7. In the event of inappropriate ZOOM courtroom behavior where any of the above-noted rules are violated; the ZOOM hearing shall be subject to termination, and a future in-court hearing shall be mandatory.  


8. In the event the Court instructs you that a mandatory in-court hearing is required and appearance on ZOOM is not permitted; should that person fail to follow that instruction and appear on ZOOM an Arrest Warrant may be issued. 










PROCEDURES WHERE NEED FOR INTERPRETOR 


Persons charged with a crime, who do not speak English are entitled by law to the services of The Court Interpreter’s Office, at no cost to the Defendant or Witnesses.  In-house Interpreters are available for those Defendants or Court Witnesses who speak Spanish, Creole or French.  For all other languages, Court Staff must Ordered seven (7) days in advance of the scheduled hearing or trial. 




PROCEDURES FOR HEARING (SCHEDULING, NOTICING CONTINUNACE AND CANCELLATION)


9.  Any request for a hearing must be in writing and filed with both Broward County Clerk of Courts and a Courtesy Copy of the Motion for continuance or Cancellation shall be transmitted via email to Judge’s Lerner-Wren’s Judicial Assistant jiovino@17th.flcourts.org  For more complex Motions, be prepared to estimate how much time is needed for the hearing. 


10. Requests for Continuance or Cancellation wherein a hearing shall be scheduled accordingly. 






COMMUNICATION WITH THE JUDGE’S OFFICE


1. Ex parte communications with the judge are strictly prohibited.  An ex parte communication occurs when a defendant, witness, or any party to a case being heard before the court attempts to directly or indirectly communicate with the judge about the case outside the knowledge of the parties. 


2. Email communication to Judge Lerner-Wren’s Judicial Assistant jiovino@17th.flcourts.org is the recommended form of communication to promote efficiency.  Email communications are answered as swiftly as possible. 






SUBMISSION OF ORDERS 


The preferred method of Submission of Orders are to Judge Lerner-Wren’s Judicial Assistant, in both PDF and WORD format should any minor corrections be necessary. (Ex. The case number, date, name of judge, or jurisdiction may need to be corrected.) 






           COURTESY COPIES 


Courtesy Copies are required to be sent to The Chambers of Judge Ginger Lerner-Wren, and to any and all opposing parties.  All Motions shall identify all parties receiving a courtesy copy. 




EMERGENCY MOTIONS AND OTHER URGENT MATTERS


Any and all requests for an Emergency Motion, Hearing or Urgent Action by the Court shall be in writing, marked or captioned as an “Emergency or Urgent Matter” and be transmitted via email to Judge Ginger Lerner-Wren’s Judicial Assistant, JoAnne Iovino, jiovino@17th.flcourts.org




For all emergency matters for those persons who are not represented by counsel, please briefly describe the nature of the emergency, and include the both a telephone contact number, and email address; and Judge Lerner-Wren’s Judicial Assistant will respond as soon as reasonably possible. 


In the event of a missed court hearing.  Please go to Broward County Clerk’s Office, and request and fill out a “Defendant’s Request Form” to request a new hearing date, and/or for example, to lift a capias if one was issued by the court for a missed court hearing.  Again, be sure to include the Case Number, and Defendant’s phone number and email address. 


EXHIBITS FOR EVIDENTIARY PROCEEDINGS 


All exhibits for evidentiary hearings must be identified and pre-marked by the Clerk prior to the start of the evidentiary hearing or trial. The parties shall review with the court if video evidence is going to be presented; and whether technical assistance is needed for court presentation purposes. 


PRETRIAL PROCEDURES AND CONFERENCES


All requests for Pretrial Motions, Hearings and Conferences shall be in writing and filed with the Clerk and Courtesy Copy sent to Judge Lerner-Wren’s Judicial Proceeding.  Any and all Motions shall be scheduled for an in-person court hearing by Judge Lerner-Wren’s Judicial Assistant. 


SETTING CASE FOR TRIAL 


Cases in Division MS are generally set for trial at the Calendar Call by The In-Court Clerk.  




PREFERRED DIVISION FORMS & OTHER DIVISION PROCEDURES FOR JAIL DIVERSION FOR MENTAL HEALTH COURT


Preferred Division Forms include Mental Health Court Transfer Orders when accepting or transferring individuals to or from Mental Health Court from other assigned misdemeanor criminal divisions.


Additional Division forms for Mental Health Court include: 
The Emergency Transportation Order, developed by the Judge Ginger Lerner-Wren along with The Broward County Public Defender’s Office Administrators. 


Emergency Transportation Order details the transportation and implements the jail diversion goals of the Mental Health Court, and to promote effective community-based discharge planning in collaboration with psychiatric acute care hospitals, and community based residential programs, and other behavioral health service providers. 
WELCOME TO BROWARD COUNTY MISDEMEANOR 
MENTAL HEALTH COURT




HISTORY, PRACTICE AND PROCEDURES




1. Broward County’s Misdemeanor Mental Health Court was established by Administrative Order No. VI-97-I-IA, issued by Chief Circuit Judge Dale Ross on June, 6th 1997.


2. Broward’s Court is the first specialized problem-solving, diversionary mental health treatment court in the United States. 


3. The Court was established to respond to the over-representation of persons arrested with serious mental illness and other co-occurring disorders; who were being arrested largely due to the lack of access to community-based mental health care, psycho-social services, supports, stigma, and lack of financing for rehabilitative programs, residential treatment programs, and supportive housing. 


4. Judge Ginger Lerner-Wren was appointed to oversee the Court based on her specialized training in disability rights, mental health systems of care, jail diversion, discharge planning, and psychiatric rehabilitation from a “person-first” approach based upon The Center for Psychiatric Rehabilitation, Boston University. 






Division MI Practice and Procedures


1. The Mental Health Court is a voluntary, diversionary, post-booking treatment court. The Court is dedicated to the promotion of community-based mental health/behavioral health treatment, wellness and recovery through the application of Therapeutic Jurisprudence aka Therapeutic Justice. 




2. In accordance with Administrative Order No. VI-97-I-IA the Mental Health Court does not hold trials. The Court handles cases involving nonviolent, misdemeanor defendants diagnosed with a serious mental illness, intellectual disability, or other neuro-cognitive disorders. (Ex. Dementia, Parkinson’s disease, Traumatic Brain Injury.) 


3. See, Video of Judge Ginger Lerner-Wren Discussing Misdemeanor Mental Health Court








MENTAL HEALTH COURT REFERRAL PROCESS 


1. Per the Administrative Order motions for transfer into the court made be made sua sponte by any court, Defense, or The State. 


2. Moreover, the Mental Health Court Referral Process is intended to be open and consumer friendly. Any person can make a referral to the court: including family members, community case managers, attorneys, probation officers, jail staff and other division judges. (No medical documentation is required.)


3. The Court’s In-Court Clinician is Janis Blenden, LCSW. Ms. Blenden has therapeutically guided the Court since 1998. Ms. Blenden is a long-time employee of Henderson Behavioral Health Center, and in private practice. 


4. To make a referral to Mental Health Court please email Judge Lerner-Wren’s Judicial Assistant, Joanne Iovino, at  jiovino@17th.flcourts.org  


5. Please include the following: The individual’s name, case number, whether the person is in jail, your phone number and email address. 


6. If the person is in-custody an in-person hearing 8:30 AM (next business day) at Broward County Courthouse, 201 SE 6th Street, Ft. Lauderdale, Fl. 33301, West Wing, 6th floor, Courtroom 6155. 




 
MENTAL HEALTH COURT HEARING PROCEDURES




7. Family, relatives and case managers may also appear by ZOOM.   




8. LINK TO ZOOM https://17thflcourts.zoom/us/j/500897463
ZOOM MEETING ID:    500 897 463 


The following rules apply to all in-person court attendees: 


1. No beverages are permitted in the courtroom


2. No children under the age of 13 years old. 


3. Cellphones must be on silent and no video recording is permitted. 


4. Appropriate attire is required for both in-court and remote hearings. 


5. If on ZOOM, all court attendees must identify themselves by their last name. Court participants shall ensure they are in appropriate settings where it is quiet, and no driving shall be permitted. 


PROCEDURES FOR ELIGIBILITY 
SCREENING, ASSESSMENT & CLINICAL TRIAGE 






   1. Every referred individual will be preliminarily screened to determine eligibility, and/or need for clinical screening, and assessment for acute care needs. 




   2. In the event of a need for medication review, or independent clinical screening for diversion; the Judge shall issue appropriate orders; including where necessary an Emergency Transportation Order requesting an independent psychiatric screening to determine need for acute care treatment and stabilization per F.S. 394.467. 


   3. Upon discharge, the Court shall be contacted to review the appropriateness of the individualized discharge plan; and continue following the progress of the court participant, and need for further services via advocacy of the court. 


   4. The court is highly individualized, and responsive to the needs of the individual based on the availability of community based resources. 


Court Jurisdiction






1. The Mental Health Court hears all adult misdemeanor offences and violation of probation matters, with the exception of DUI’s and Domestic Violence cases and Battery charges are accepted with victim’s consent (subject to court approval).




2. Because it was designed to deal with people who, because of their illness, return frequently to the criminal justice system, the court accepts defendants with prior convictions. 




3. The Court targets individuals with non-violent, low level misdemeanor offenses, but will consider criminal histories which include violent crimes, which are carefully screened to avoid those who pose a significant threat to public safety. 






PROCEDURE: COMPETENCY TO STAND TRIAL 


1. When a defendant is believed to be incompetent, due process requires the Court to order an evaluation. 






2. If he or she is found incompetent, the court shall order a conditional release plan be developed subject to treatment and supervision based upon an individual’s social and psychiatric level of care needs. Note, the court strives to honor preferences. 


3. A defendant who is found Incompetent to Proceed to Trial and has no place to live is placed in the court’s transitional housing facility, Henderson Rainbow Villas or other community program based on availability. 


4. The Court maintains jurisdiction over the defendant’s case for 12 months during which time the court monitors his or her compliance with the release conditions and receives periodic reports on his progress. 




5. If the Defendant remains incompetent, the charges are subject to dismissal per Florida Rules of Criminal Procedure.






GOALS OF BROWARD’S MENTAL HEALTH COURT 




1. To create effective interactions between the criminal justice and mental health systems, including legal advocacy for the mentally ill defendant. 


2. To ensure that mentally ill offenders do not languish in jail because of their illness. 


3. To balance the legal rights of the defendant with the need for public safety by recommending the least restrictive and most appropriate, workable disposition. 


4. Reduce mentally ill defendants’ contact with the criminal justice system.




5. To divert mentally ill offenders to community based mental health services, including monitoring of mental health care delivery. 


6. A focus on recovery by promoting consumer and family participation and education through the court process.




VALUES AND PRINCIPLES OF THE COURT 




1.  The Mental Health Court is a collaborative court. It is the outgrowth of the Grand Jury Report of 1994 and the work of the Ad Hoc Criminal Justice and Mental Health Task Force formed at this time. This diverse assembly of criminal justice and mental health stakeholders worked tirelessly for several years seeking solutions to improve the streamlining of people entering the jail system with serious mental illness.
2.  Former Broward County Public Defender, Howard Finkelstein, was the brain child of the concept for a specialized mental health court and envisioned a court which would promote dignity and respect as well as having a specialization in psychiatric rehabilitation and disability rights.




3. The court wholly adopts the legal philosophy of Therapeutic Jurisprudence, which is based on the Three V’s: Voluntariness, Voice and Validation of the court participants. (Ronner, A. Donner, Songs of Validation, Voice, and Voluntary Participation: Therapeutic Jurisprudence, Miranda and Juveniles, 71 U.CIN. L. REV. 89, 94-95 (2002).








MENTAL HEALTH COURT SPECIAL RECOGNITIONS 


1. The Court was showcased at The White House Conference on Mental Health, 1999. 




2. Broward’s Court was the model for the American Law Enforcement and Mental Health Project passed by Congress in October, 2000 and signed into law by President Clinton on November 13, 2000, to fund 100 mental health courts across the United States.








3.  The Court is the model for the one of four the U.S. Department of Justice looked at in 2000 report on “Emerging Judicial Strategies for the Mentally Ill in Criminal Caseloads.” The report is available at https://www.ncjrs.org/pdffiles1/bja/182504.pdf.




4. The Court was selected as “Top 3 Finalists” 2013 Innovating Justice Awards, The HiiL Foundation, The Hague, The Netherlands. 


5. Judge Lerner-Wren received the “Excellence in Advocacy Awards for Elected Service, 2015 National Council for Wellbeing. 


6. The Court has been honored nationally and internationally for Court Innovation and the humane treatment of persons with mental illness and co-occurring substance use disorders as well as other cognitive disabilities. On the Court’s 20th Anniversary  the achievements of the community was recognized in the Congressional Record by U.S. Representative Alcee Hastings on June 13, 2017.




7. President George W. Bush, appointed Judge Lerner-Wren to serve on The President’s New Freedom Commission, CJ Sub-committee Chair, 2002-2003.

County Court Civil and Criminal
COUNTY COURT CIVIL
The County Civil division has jurisdiction over most landlord-tenant disputes, as well as civil matters in which the value of property, debt or other issue of controversy is between $8,001 and $50,000. These cases typically include personal injury protection and other insurance disputes; condominium and homeowner association disputes; repossession and replevin actions; and small claims cases. The County Civil Division has judges assigned at courthouses throughout Broward County, including the West Tower in downtown Fort Lauderdale, as well as regional locations in Deerfield Beach, Hollywood, and Plantation.
Video of Judge Jennifer Hilal Discussing County Civil Eviction Cases
Small claims cases involve cases over property or unpaid bills with a value up to $8,000 (excluding court costs, interest and/or attorney’s fees, if applicable). Small claims lawsuits may be filed by individuals or businesses. Special rules of procedure (
Small Claims Rules)
are designed to make the court process simpler, speedier and more informal than the regular civil court process. For info on small claims court
Click Here
.
Judge Kathleen McCarthy Discusses Small Claims
COUNTY COURT CRIMINAL DIVISION
The County Court Criminal Division handles criminal misdemeanor cases, criminal traffic matters, municipal and county ordinance violations and civil traffic infractions. Criminal misdemeanor cases include violations of the law such as Petit Theft, Simple Battery and Trespassing. Criminal Traffic matters include violations such as Driving While License Suspended, Driving under the Influence and no Valid Driver’s License cases.
Misdemeanor and Criminal Traffic matters are heard by county court judges. First degree misdemeanors are punishable by imprisonment of up to a year in the county jail and a fine of up to $1,000.00. Second degree misdemeanors are punishable by imprisonment of up to 60 days in the county jail and a fine of up to $500.00. Driving under the Influence has its own penalty provisions, which are mandated by law.
Civil Traffic infractions, which are non-criminal related violations, are generally heard by Civil Traffic Hearing Officers and consist of moving and non-moving violations. Moving violations, such as speeding and running a red light, may result in an assessment of points on your license. Other non-moving violations, such as expired registration or no seat belt, do not result in points assessed against your license.
Judge Kenneth A. Gottlieb and Judge Deborah Carpenter-Toye Discussing County Court Criminal Division
The County Court Criminal Judiciary and their staff are located at the Broward County Central Courthouse, 201 SE. 6th Street, Ft. Lauderdale, Fla. 33301 and at the three satellite courthouses located in Hollywood, Plantation
and Deerfield Beach.

County Court Civil and Criminal
COUNTY COURT CIVIL
The County Civil division has jurisdiction over most landlord-tenant disputes, as well as civil matters in which the value of property, debt or other issue of controversy is between $8,001 and $50,000. These cases typically include personal injury protection and other insurance disputes; condominium and homeowner association disputes; repossession and replevin actions; and small claims cases. The County Civil Division has judges assigned at courthouses throughout Broward County, including the West Tower in downtown Fort Lauderdale, as well as regional locations in Deerfield Beach, Hollywood, and Plantation.
Video of Judge Jennifer Hilal Discussing County Civil Eviction Cases
Small claims cases involve cases over property or unpaid bills with a value up to $8,000 (excluding court costs, interest and/or attorney’s fees, if applicable). Small claims lawsuits may be filed by individuals or businesses. Special rules of procedure (
Small Claims Rules)
are designed to make the court process simpler, speedier and more informal than the regular civil court process. For info on small claims court
Click Here
.
Judge Kathleen McCarthy Discusses Small Claims
COUNTY COURT CRIMINAL DIVISION
The County Court Criminal Division handles criminal misdemeanor cases, criminal traffic matters, municipal and county ordinance violations and civil traffic infractions. Criminal misdemeanor cases include violations of the law such as Petit Theft, Simple Battery and Trespassing. Criminal Traffic matters include violations such as Driving While License Suspended, Driving under the Influence and no Valid Driver’s License cases.
Misdemeanor and Criminal Traffic matters are heard by county court judges. First degree misdemeanors are punishable by imprisonment of up to a year in the county jail and a fine of up to $1,000.00. Second degree misdemeanors are punishable by imprisonment of up to 60 days in the county jail and a fine of up to $500.00. Driving under the Influence has its own penalty provisions, which are mandated by law.
Civil Traffic infractions, which are non-criminal related violations, are generally heard by Civil Traffic Hearing Officers and consist of moving and non-moving violations. Moving violations, such as speeding and running a red light, may result in an assessment of points on your license. Other non-moving violations, such as expired registration or no seat belt, do not result in points assessed against your license.
Judge Kenneth A. Gottlieb and Judge Deborah Carpenter-Toye Discussing County Court Criminal Division
The County Court Criminal Judiciary and their staff are located at the Broward County Central Courthouse, 201 SE. 6th Street, Ft. Lauderdale, Fla. 33301 and at the three satellite courthouses located in Hollywood, Plantation
and Deerfield Beach.

** Seminole Division W, hearings will only proceed if all exhibits/documents for the Court's consideration are electronically filed 72 hours in advance of the hearing. Noncompliance will result in cancellation or rescheduling of the hearing. A notary must be present to identify the witnesses and place them under an oath to tell the truth. **
What is Circuit Court?
Circuit - Trial Courts
What is a circuit?
There are 20 judicial circuits in the Florida court system. Brevard and Seminole make up the Eighteenth Circuit. Circuit courts have general trial jurisdiction over matters not assigned by statute to the county courts and also hear appeals from county court cases. Some circuits are made up of multiple counties.
Close
What is County Court?
County Trial Courts
What County Courts Do?
The Florida Constitution establishes that there is ONE county court in each of Florida’s 67 counties. The county courts are sometimes referred to as "the people's courts," probably because a large part of the courts' work involves voluminous citizen disputes, such as traffic offenses, less serious criminal matters (misdemeanors), and relatively small monetary disputes.
Close
What is are Magistrates?
General Magistrates & Hearing Officers
What do they do?
General Magistrates
are responsible for cases involving:
Temporary relief (alimony, child support, and attorneys fees and costs in family law cases)
Contempt of court
Support enforcement
Mental health (Baker Act)
Substance abuse (Marchman Act)
Tuberculosis and Sexually transmissible diseases
Incapacity
Guardianship (including guardian applications, background investigations and annual reports filed with the court)
Modification of prior rulings
Dependency review hearings
As part of the Guardianship Law, General Magistrates assist the Probate Court with guardian application and background checks, and plenary and limited guardianships.
Hearing Officers
are appointed to hear Family Division cases dealing with family support issues. The Findings and Recommendations entered by the Hearing Officer have the same force and effect as Orders entered by a Circuit Judge.
Close

Magistrates & Hearing Officers
General Magistrates
The General Magistrate is an attorney appointed by the Chief Circuit Judge to hear certain types of cases, which include family law, civil, foreclosure, mental health, dependency, early childhood court, and truancy, and make findings based upon the evidence presented. The findings are reduced to writing in a Recommended Order for family law cases or a Report and Recommendation for all other cases. This report is basically the General Magistrates suggestion for a ruling in a particular case. If neither party files a timely Motion to Vacate the General Magistrates Recommended Order or an Exception to the General Magistrates Report and Recommendation, the Judge assigned to the case will review the Recommended Order or Report and Recommendation and if he or she is in agreement with the findings, they will enter an order approving the Recommended Order or Report and Recommendation.

Taylor County
was created in 1856. It was named for Zachary Taylor, twelfth President of the United States. Its county seat is Perry. Taylor County is home to nearly 60 miles of coastline, four rivers (Econfina, Aucilla, Fenholloway, and Steinhatchee Rivers), numerous streams and creeks, springs, a border on the Apalachee Bay, both natural and artificial reefs and quick access to the Gulf of Mexico. The county has a total area of 1,232 square miles, of which 1,043 square miles is land and 189 square miles (15.3%) is water.

The Code of Judicial Conduct governing behavior by judges forbids judges from discussing pending cases with the public or parties to cases. What is Circuit Court?
Circuit - Trial Courts
What is a circuit?
There are 20 judicial circuits in the Florida court system. Brevard and Seminole make up the Eighteenth Circuit. Circuit courts have general trial jurisdiction over matters not assigned by statute to the county courts and also hear appeals from county court cases. Some circuits are made up of multiple counties.
Close
What is County Court?
County Trial Courts
What County Courts Do?
The Florida Constitution establishes that there is ONE county court in each of Florida’s 67 counties. The county courts are sometimes referred to as "the people's courts," probably because a large part of the courts' work involves voluminous citizen disputes, such as traffic offenses, less serious criminal matters (misdemeanors), and relatively small monetary disputes.
Close
What is are Magistrates?
General Magistrates & Hearing Officers
What do they do?
General Magistrates
are responsible for cases involving:
Temporary relief (alimony, child support, and attorneys fees and costs in family law cases)
Contempt of court
Support enforcement
Mental health (Baker Act)
Substance abuse (Marchman Act)
Tuberculosis and Sexually transmissible diseases
Incapacity
Guardianship (including guardian applications, background investigations and annual reports filed with the court)
Modification of prior rulings
Dependency review hearings
As part of the Guardianship Law, General Magistrates assist the Probate Court with guardian application and background checks, and plenary and limited guardianships.
Hearing Officers
are appointed to hear Family Division cases dealing with family support issues. The Findings and Recommendations entered by the Hearing Officer have the same force and effect as Orders entered by a Circuit Judge.

Eighteenth Judicial Circuit Courts Judicial Directory

** Seminole Division W, hearings will only proceed if all exhibits/documents for the Court's consideration are electronically filed 72 hours in advance of the hearing. Noncompliance will result in cancellation or rescheduling of the hearing. A notary must be present to identify the witnesses and place them under an oath to tell the truth. **
What is Circuit Court?
Circuit - Trial Courts
What is a circuit?
There are 20 judicial circuits in the Florida court system. Brevard and Seminole make up the Eighteenth Circuit. Circuit courts have general trial jurisdiction over matters not assigned by statute to the county courts and also hear appeals from county court cases. Some circuits are made up of multiple counties.
Close
What is County Court?
County Trial Courts
What County Courts Do?
The Florida Constitution establishes that there is ONE county court in each of Florida’s 67 counties. The county courts are sometimes referred to as "the people's courts," probably because a large part of the courts' work involves voluminous citizen disputes, such as traffic offenses, less serious criminal matters (misdemeanors), and relatively small monetary disputes.
Close
What is are Magistrates?
General Magistrates & Hearing Officers
What do they do?
General Magistrates
are responsible for cases involving:
Temporary relief (alimony, child support, and attorneys fees and costs in family law cases)
Contempt of court
Support enforcement
Mental health (Baker Act)
Substance abuse (Marchman Act)
Tuberculosis and Sexually transmissible diseases
Incapacity
Guardianship (including guardian applications, background investigations and annual reports filed with the court)
Modification of prior rulings
Dependency review hearings
As part of the Guardianship Law, General Magistrates assist the Probate Court with guardian application and background checks, and plenary and limited guardianships.
Hearing Officers
are appointed to hear Family Division cases dealing with family support issues. The Findings and Recommendations entered by the Hearing Officer have the same force and effect as Orders entered by a Circuit Judge.

Judges Directory
Eighteenth Judicial Circuit Courts Judicial Directory
NOTE: Not all of the judges post their calendars online. Calendars are subject to change hourly, so check back frequently to guarantee accurate updates.
** Seminole Division W, hearings will only proceed if all exhibits/documents for the Court's consideration are electronically filed 72 hours in advance of the hearing. Noncompliance will result in cancellation or rescheduling of the hearing. A notary must be present to identify the witnesses and place them under an oath to tell the truth. **
What is Circuit Court?
Circuit - Trial Courts
What is a circuit?
There are 20 judicial circuits in the Florida court system. Brevard and Seminole make up the Eighteenth Circuit. Circuit courts have general trial jurisdiction over matters not assigned by statute to the county courts and also hear appeals from county court cases. Some circuits are made up of multiple counties.
Close
What is County Court?
County Trial Courts
What County Courts Do?
The Florida Constitution establishes that there is ONE county court in each of Florida’s 67 counties. The county courts are sometimes referred to as "the people's courts," probably because a large part of the courts' work involves voluminous citizen disputes, such as traffic offenses, less serious criminal matters (misdemeanors), and relatively small monetary disputes.
Close
What is are Magistrates?
General Magistrates & Hearing Officers
What do they do?
General Magistrates
are responsible for cases involving:
Temporary relief (alimony, child support, and attorneys fees and costs in family law cases)
Contempt of court
Support enforcement
Mental health (Baker Act)
Substance abuse (Marchman Act)
Tuberculosis and Sexually transmissible diseases
Incapacity
Guardianship (including guardian applications, background investigations and annual reports filed with the court)
Modification of prior rulings
Dependency review hearings
As part of the Guardianship Law, General Magistrates assist the Probate Court with guardian application and background checks, and plenary and limited guardianships.
Hearing Officers
are appointed to hear Family Division cases dealing with family support issues. The Findings and Recommendations entered by the Hearing Officer have the same force and effect as Orders entered by a Circuit Judge.
Close

** Seminole Division W, hearings will only proceed if all exhibits/documents for the Court's consideration are electronically filed 72 hours in advance of the hearing. Noncompliance will result in cancellation or rescheduling of the hearing. A notary must be present to identify the witnesses and place them under an oath to tell the truth. **
What is Circuit Court?
Circuit - Trial Courts
What is a circuit?
There are 20 judicial circuits in the Florida court system. Brevard and Seminole make up the Eighteenth Circuit. Circuit courts have general trial jurisdiction over matters not assigned by statute to the county courts and also hear appeals from county court cases. Some circuits are made up of multiple counties.
Close
What is County Court?
County Trial Courts
What County Courts Do?
The Florida Constitution establishes that there is ONE county court in each of Florida’s 67 counties. The county courts are sometimes referred to as "the people's courts," probably because a large part of the courts' work involves voluminous citizen disputes, such as traffic offenses, less serious criminal matters (misdemeanors), and relatively small monetary disputes.
Close
What is are Magistrates?
General Magistrates & Hearing Officers
What do they do?
General Magistrates
are responsible for cases involving:
Temporary relief (alimony, child support, and attorneys fees and costs in family law cases)
Contempt of court
Support enforcement
Mental health (Baker Act)
Substance abuse (Marchman Act)
Tuberculosis and Sexually transmissible diseases
Incapacity
Guardianship (including guardian applications, background investigations and annual reports filed with the court)
Modification of prior rulings
Dependency review hearings
As part of the Guardianship Law, General Magistrates assist the Probate Court with guardian application and background checks, and plenary and limited guardianships.
Hearing Officers
are appointed to hear Family Division cases dealing with family support issues. The Findings and Recommendations entered by the Hearing Officer have the same force and effect as Orders entered by a Circuit Judge.

Holly Aliprandi – General Magistrate Instructions
Table of Contents

A. Submission of Recommended Orders and Reports and Recommendations
Format:
All proposed recommended orders and proposed reports and recommendations must be submitted in Word format and provided to opposing counsel and any self-represented litigant.
All proposed recommended orders and proposed reports and recommendations must be accompanied by a cover letter either:
certifying that all parties agree to the proposed recommended order or report
OR
containing a statement identifying any disagreement of the parties as to the proposed recommended order or report.
Submission Method:
All proposed recommended orders and reports and recommendations must be submitted to the court by the proposed order portion of the Florida Courts E-Filing Portal
Deadline for Submissions:
Proposed orders must be submitted no later than
five (5)
days after any hearing unless otherwise instructed.
B. Courtesy Copies of Case Law & Other Documents
When Required:
Courtesy copies of
Case Law and Exhibits for Trial and Evidentiary Hearings
the party wishes the court to consider must be submitted to the court for any hearing or trial.
Courtesy copies must be submitted in PDF/a format.
Submission Method:
Courtesy copies must be submitted to the Court by e-mail to the appropriate case manager.
Deadline for Submission:
Courtesy copies must be submitted to the court no later than
Five (5)
days before any hearing or trial.
C. Exhibits for Evidentiary Proceedings
Submission Methods:
Unless otherwise instructed, Copies of exhibits and exhibit lists shall be forwarded to the appropriate case manager via e-mail at least five (5) business days prior to the scheduled hearing. Please note, the Clerk of Court requires hard copies of exhibits, marked with
letters
for identification, which shall be submitted at least five (5) business days prior to the scheduled hearings. Numbered exhibits will not be accepted. Numbered exhibits will ONLY be accepted if they are stipulated to.
Format:
Exhibits must be labeled in the following format:
All attorneys and self-represented litigants must provide copies of each exhibit for the clerk, the court, and each party prior to the hearing or trial.
D. Remote Hearings
Zoom Meeting Information
Zoom meeting ID: 989 1485 6399 and No Passcode
https://zoom.us/s/98914856399
Pursuant Rule of General Practice and Judicial Administration 2.530, certain court proceedings may continue to be conducted remotely via audio-video conferencing through “Zoom”.  Generally, this division schedules the following matters to be conducted via Zoom:  Uniform Motion Calendar hearings, Child Support Calendar hearings, hearings under two hours, and any hearings specifically requested by motion and granted.  All hearings conducted via Zoom will be audio-recorded.
Before the Day of Your Hearing
You will need an electronic device such as a desktop or laptop computer, smartphone, or tablet that has a camera and microphone, an email account, and a reliable internet connection.
ALL USERS MUST BE ABLE TO CONNECT TO AUDIO AND VIDEO AND MUST BE ABLE TO USE THEIR MICROPHONE FOR HEARINGS.
For desktop computers and laptops, you will not need to download the Zoom software. Using a desktop computer or laptop, go to
https://zoom.us/
and click join in the top right corner of the screen. To ensure that you will be able to smoothly join the hearing before the day of, enter the Zoom meeting ID and try to join the meeting.
Using a mobile device, find the Zoom app in the Play Store for Android devices or in the App Store for Apple Devices. Download the app to install it to your device. Once the application for your mobile device is installed, open the app and create an account. After logging in, you will be able to use Zoom for free. To ensure that you will be able to smoothly join the hearing before the day of, enter the Zoom meeting ID and try to join the meeting.
If you are unable to use the Zoom application, you may dial in on your phone to connect to the call. This is
NOT
permitted, however, for Final Hearings or Evidentiary Hearings. Find your local number:
https://zoom.us/u/adwMoy4YjM
and when prompted to enter an ID, enter #98914856399 to enter the hearing.
Your Zoom participant name
MUST
reflect your full legal name so that you may be properly identified and routed by the General Magistrate.
Allow enough time in advance of your hearing to familiarize yourself with how to use Zoom.
On the Day of Your Hearing
To ensure you have a good connection, please connect to the Zoom hearing at least 10 minutes before the hearing is scheduled to begin.
Please be aware that other hearings may be going on while you are in the waiting room and that the previous hearing may go over their allotted time. If you have been waiting for more than 10 minutes past your scheduled hearing time, reach out to the case manager to ensure you are in the right Zoom meeting and that the wait is solely because of the hearing before yours.
When your hearing is called, the Magistrate will admit you to the hearing. You will then be prompted to connect to audio and turn on your camera. Unless you are connected to audio, we will not be able to hear you and therefor cannot conduct the hearing.
Please be mindful that although it is a Zoom meeting, you are still in Court and should act and dress appropriately. Minimize sound in the background, be seated and present, and
DO NOT
be operating a vehicle during the hearing.
Consequences for a failure to appear:
A court hearing held on Zoom, like a court hearing held in person, is an official court event subject to consequences for a failure to appear at the hearing. If you fail to appear at your properly noticed hearing on Zoom, the consequences, depending on the type of case, may include, but are not limited to, one or more of the following:
Cancellation of your hearing.
Conduct and resolution of the hearing without your participation.
Dismissal of your case if you are a petitioner or counter-petitioner (i.e., the person who file a petition or counter-petition).
Entry of a judgment against you (referred to as a “default judgment”) if you are a defendant (i.e., the person who is sued).
Penalties such as fines, jail time, and suspension of your driver’s license.

Judicial Assistant:   Ja milah (Jay ) Simmons  - email: simmonsj@circuit19.org  
Assignment:   All St Lucie County Civil Cases (designated with a “CC”, “EV”, or “TR” case number and Small 
Claims Cases (designated with a “SC” and a case number ending in 3, 6 or 9  ) 
No hearing should be scheduled against a n opposing attorney unless the m otion has been filed or tendered to 
opposing counsel, discussed  to attempt resolution , AND the date and time are coordinated.   If more than two 
attempts, spread out over at least 4 business days, have been made by phone AND email , without a reply, then 
counsel may unilaterally  set their hearing.   All notices of hearing should certify what attempts were made to 
resolve and coordinate.  
Scheduling can be done online for any hearing that will last less than one hour of time.  There is no need to call 
my JA to  schedule a hearing unless there is no date available, with sufficient time for your motion(s) , within 
the next 60 days.  My calendar may be found online on the 19th Circuit’s Website under Judges and 
Magistrates , or at the following link: https://slccjis.stlucieco.gov/attorney_calendar/  Most  open dates on my 
calendar are designated either UMC or Special S et.   UMC are for routine  matters (often motions for extension 
of time, or  to amend  or withdraw ) that can be argued by BOTH sides and ruled on in 10 minutes or less, and 
are usually found on Tuesday mornings.  Telephonic  appearance at an UMC hearing is always permissible 
through Court Call.  You do not need a motion and order to appear by tele phone at an UMC hearing.   On the 
other hand, Special Set hearings  are usually found on Thursday afternoons and  require personal appearance , 
or require a motion and order to appear by telephone.  If telephonic appearance at a Special Set hearing is granted , it will always require the use of Court Call , and applies to both sides equally (in other words, the 
proposed order should state that if it’s granted, either party may appear telephonically via Court Call).   Specia l 
Set hearings are reserved for longer,  more complicated matters  (often cross -set or evidentiary motions, 
motions to strike or compel , motions for summary judgment  or for attorney’s fees, or pretrial conferences)  
that will require anywhere from 10 -60 minutes  for argument and a ruling .   
All original pleadings, stipulations, motions , and notices must be filed with the Clerk or eportal.  Additionally , 
all parties are required  to also mail (US Mail or overnight carrier – do not email) copies  of the notice of hearing, 
motion, relevant pleadings, suf ficient proposed orders (one original plus a copy for each party that does not 
already have an email address designated on the eportal), and stamped envelopes (again one for each party 
that does not already have an email address designated on the eportal)  to my attention at least 5 days prior to 
hearing.  The Court reserves the right to cancel any hearing , or to enter an exparte order reversing an order 
orally pronounced at any hearing, without proposed orders and stamped envelopes provided in advance for immediate entry .   
No attorneys may appear at any trial, eviction or claim of exemption hearing, or case management conference 
by telephone  (unless Covid restrictions are in place) .  Witnesses may be permitted to appear by telephone 
after motion and order, by Court Call only, and in compliance with FRCP 1.451.   Stipulations of any kind must 
be filed, but a SEPARATE, proposed order approving, may be sent via email, copied to opposing counsel. Filing 
a stipulation does not cancel a trial or case management con ference.  An order approving the stipulation is 
required to cancel a previously ORDERED hearing or trial (including pretrial in SMALL CLAIMS CASES ).   
Additionally, p roposed orders to invoke the FRCP in small claims cases must retain Small Claims Rule 7.13 5 
AND MUST BE ACCOMPANIED BY A PROPOSED CASE MANANGEMENT PLAN AND ORDER in c ompliance with 
AOSC20 -23 and AO 2021- 05 (see Forms) . ALL COUNTY CIVIL CASES WILL ALSO REQUIRE A CASE MANAGEMENT 
PLAN TO BE FILED BY PLAINITFF within 90 days , unless defendant is represented by an attorney.  In those 
cases, defendant is responsible for coordinating and submitting a  proposed ca se management plan within 30  
days of their appearance.

Howard Coates, Jr. Circuit Judge

205 N. Dixie Highway, Room 10.2204
