Volusia County
Volusia County Courthouse
101 N. Alabama Ave.
DeLand, FL  32724
The Volusia County Courthouse, opened in 2001.  The courthouse is made of precast concrete with a brick facade. The building contains many interesting architectural features, most notably, a clock tower with a seal of Lady Justice.
S. James Foxman Justice Center
251 N. Ridgewood Ave.
Daytona Beach, FL  32114
The Volusia County Justice Center, completed in 1990, is a three story octagon shaped structure. Volusia County was the first county in Florida to use a design/build process in constructing a courthouse. The courthouse was designed with security high technology and aesthetics in mind.
Steven C. Henderson Judicial Center
125 E. Orange Ave.
Daytona Beach, FL 32114
The Steven C. Henderson Judicial Center was built in 1970 to fill the needs of the county’s growing eastern population. The courthouse is in a beautiful location on the Halifax River. The three story building is of modern design.

If the request is being made less than 14 days prior to the scheduled hearing, or if a party is not in agreement with the request for a continuance/reset, the Moving/Requesting-Party
must file a motion to continue detailing the reason for the request, and follow the procedural steps below:
The Moving/Requesting-Party must request a hearing date and time for their Motion to be heard, via email at CAD- JRScheduling@pbcgov.org with a copy of the motion attached.
Hearings on Motions to Continue will be heard on Tuesdays and Thursdays between the times of
8:30 AM – 9:00 AM only
via Zoom.
It is the requesting-party's responsibility to coordinate with the parties regarding the date and time provided by the Magistrate's Assistant, and subsequently report back with the results of availability. The parties shall not reply piecemeal regarding their individual availability.
Once the Magistrate's Assistant confirms the date and time is still available, the Movant/requesting-party shall prepare and file a notice of hearing. Once filed, a courtesy copy shall be sent to the Magistrate's Assistant.
Interpreters
It is the responsibility of the party who requires an interpreter to make arrangements for one to attend a scheduled Hearing.
Please make all interpreter services requests at

Judges

The First Judicial Circuit includes Escambia, Santa Rosa, Okaloosa, and Walton Counties. Twenty-six circuit judges and twelve county judges serve within the Circuit and are assisted by general magistrates and hearing officers in hearing and disposing of cases. Judges are elected by the voters of the Circuit in non-partisan elections and serve for six-year terms.

Circuit judges handle all circuit court cases, including felony criminal, domestic relations (family), probate, guardianship, juvenile (both dependency and delinquency), and civil suits in which more than $50,000 is at issue.

County court judges handle county court cases, including misdemeanor criminal, landlord-tenant, small claims, traffic, and civil suits in which $50,000 or less is at issue.

Under the Florida Code of Judicial Conduct, judges cannot speak to parties or members of the public regarding pending cases. Judges are permitted to consider arguments made only during court proceedings and in documents filed by parties in a case.

Judicial Practices and Procedures  FELONY DIVISION F 5 
 
If you are represented by an attorney , you must  contact your  
attorney directly with any questions and/or concerns.  
 
John C. Waters , Judge  
Miranda Brook s, Judicial Assistant  
 
Contact Information  
Mailing Address: P.O. Box 9000, Drawer J -116, Bartow, FL 33831 -9000  
Telephone: 863-534-4645  
Fax: 863-534-7724  
 
MOTIONS/JSEL/TRIAL COURTROOM:  6A (sixth  floor, red elevators)  
ARRAIGNMENT COURTROOM:  Main Courtroom (first floor)  
PRETRIAL CONFERENCE COURTROOM:  Courtroom 4A (fourth floor, red 
elevators)  
ADMINISTRATIVE ORDERS:  Copies of all Administrative Orders for the Tenth 
Judicial Circuit are available here: Administrative Order Divisions | 10th 
Judicial Circuit Court  
 
Table of Contents  
A. Communications with the Judicial Office  ................................ ...............  pg. 1  
B. Scheduling Procedures  ................................ ................................ ...... pg. 2-3 
C. Court Appearance s ................................ ................................ ............  pg. 3 -4 
D. Submission of Motions  and proposed Orders  ................................ ..... pg. 4 -5 
E. Memorandums and Courtesy Copies of Case Law  ................................ .. pg. 5 
F. Emergency and other Urgent Matters  ................................ ....................  pg. 5 
G. Mandatory Docketing  ................................ ................................ ............  pg. 5  
H. Early Termination of Probation  ................................ ..............................  pg. 6 
I. Other Division Procedures  ................................ ................................ ..... pg. 6 
  
Page 1 of 11 A. Communications with the Judicial Office  
• Method of Communication : Communications to the judicial office must 
be submitted by e -mail to Brinna Allbritton , Judicial Assistant at 
mbrooks@Jud10.FLCourts.org . The subject line of any e -mail to the 
judicial office must contain the case number, case name, and relevant 
matter (e.g., 2024 DR 001234 SC – Doe v. Doe – 2-Hour Hearing 
Requested). On occasion, it may be necessary to communicate with the 
judicial office via telephone. The judicial office may be contacted via 
telephone at 863 -534-4149. The judicial office may request a follow up e -
mail to any telephonic communication . The judicial office does not accept 
text messages.  
• Ex parte communications : All communications with the judicial office 
must comply with  Canon 3 of the Code of Judicial Conduct, which 
prohibits a judge  from initiating, permitting, or considering ex parte 
communications and from considering other communications outside the 
presence of the parties concerning a pending or impending proceeding, 
unless authorized by law. All parties must be copied on any e -mail directed 
to the judicial office, unless an ex parte communication is authorized by 
law. 
• Unsolicited Communications : Parties may only contact the judicial office 
in accordance with these practices and procedures. Unsolicited 
communications from non -parties will not be considered by the court . 
• E-Filing Portal Contact Information : All attorneys and self -represented 
litigants must make and receive  service by e -mail, which is generally 
through the Florida Courts E -Filing Portal, unless excused. Fla. R. Gen. 
Prac. & Jud. Admin. 2.516. It is the responsibility of attorneys and self -
represented litigants to update their contact information using Form 2.603 
any time there is a change in the e -mail account registered for electronic 
service.  
• Response to Inquiries : The judicial assistant strives to substantively 
respond to all inquiries within one business day. If the judicial assistant 
is unable to substantively respond within one business day, your message 
will be acknowledged as received with an indication of whe n to expect a 
substantive response or an alternate contact for immediate assistance. 
The judicial assistant is not authorized to provide legal advice . 
• Any e -mail sent to or from the judicial office is a public record  subject to 
disclosure.  
 
Page 2 of 11 B. Scheduling Procedures  
• Court Schedule : FelonyMasterCalendar.pdf  
• Scheduling Hearings : E-mail the Judicial Assistant at, 
mbrooks@Jud10.FLCourts.org  to obtain hearing times for your Motion . 
Such requests must include the case number, Defendant’s name, 
matter(s) to be heard, and time required. The party scheduling the hearing 
is responsible for contacting all other parties  and coordinating an agreed 
upon date and time . DO NOT include the Judicial Assistant in any 
electronic communications with other parties relating to the 
coordination of the hearing . The hearing times provided are not held 
while the attempt is being made to coordinate with opposing 
counsel/party. You must e -mail the judicial office to  confirm and reserve 
your court date prior to submitting your Notice of Hearing.  
• Notice of Hearing : Upon confirmation from the Judicial Assistant, the 
scheduling party must file and immediately  serve a Notice of Hearing . The 
scheduling party must also send a copy of the Notice of Hearing to the 
Judicial Assistant. Failure to follow these procedures will result in the 
hearing not being added to the docket. All notices of hearing must contain 
the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) notification required by Florida 
Rule of General Practice and Judicial Administration 2.540.  
• Cancelling Hearings : You must cancel hearings by notifying the Judicial 
Assistant immediately. After a hearing is set , opposing counsel must 
consent to the cancellation. You must also immediately file and serve a 
notice of cancellation on opposing counsel and any self -represented 
litigant.  
• Submission Deadlines : The Court must receive all materials for the 
hearing no later than three (3) business days before the hearing.  
• Order of Proceedings : Sounding of the docket is at the Court’s 
discretion.  
• Continuance Procedure : Motions for continuance are disfavored and will 
be granted only upon good cause shown. Successive continuances are 
highly disfavored. Lack of due diligence is not grounds for granting a 
continuance. Except for good cause shown, the motion must be signed by 
the party requesting the continuance, as required by Florida Rule of 
General Practice and Judicial Administration 2.545(e).  
• Motions for Continuance of Pretrial Conference/Arraignment : An 
agreed upon Motion for Continuance of Pretrial Conference or Arraignment 
Page 3 of 11 and a proposed Order  must be submitted no later than 1:00 p.m. three  (3) 
business days prior to scheduled hearing. Otherwise, the hearing will 
remain on the docket and will be addressed in Court at the scheduled time. 
The Court may still require a hearing on an agreed upon Motion for 
Continuance . 
• Waiver of Status Conference in Polk Felony Division F 2: Defense 
counsel may waive a regularly scheduled status conference in Polk Felony 
Divisions F4 by filing a document titled Waiver of Status Conference , 
reflecting that the Defendant is waiving the status conference and 
requesting the case be passed to the previously scheduled Pretrial 
Conference. The Waiver of Status Conference  must be signed by counsel 
for the Defendant and served on the assigned attorney for the State and 
the assigned judge’s Judicial  Assistant. The Judicial Assistant must not 
be added to the e -service list but served by separate e -mail. The Waiver of 
Status Conference  must be filed and served no later than close of business 
two business days prior to the scheduled status conference. (e.g., 5:00 
p.m. on Wednesday for a Friday morning status conference). See Exhibit 
A for a Sample Waiver of Status Conference.  
C. Court  Appearance s 
• Pursuant to Administrative Order 1 -60.0, (subject to change) effective 
June 21, 2021, criminal proceedings will be conducted in-person  
unless otherwise notified by counsel and/or approved by the judge.  
• IN-PERSON APPEARANCE : All defendants MUST appear in -person for 
all hearings unless a waiver of appearance has been filed.  The 
Defendant MUST be present for mandatory docketing; counsel cannot 
waive the Defendant’s presence for Mandatory Docketing.  
• REMOTE APPEARANCE : If a need arises for a remote appearance of 
counsel or a witness, a written Motion  and proposed Order  to appear 
virtually must  be submitted to the court  no later than three  (3)business  
days prior to the scheduled hearing or the Motion  will not be considered.  
• Remote Appearance Procedure : The Court will call the cases of the 
attorneys physically present in the courtroom first.  
▪ Platform Used : Microsoft Teams  
▪ Technology Needs : The answers to the most frequently asked 
questions regarding technology needs can be found at the 
following link:  
How to Access the 1 0th Circuit  Teams Virtual  Courtroom  
Page 4 of 11 For any inquiries regarding technology needs, contact Court I.T. 
at 863-534-7788 . 
▪ Rules for remote appearance : Any person appearing remotely 
must be in a private location that is quiet and free from 
distractions. Under no circumstances will a participant be 
permitted to appear remotely from a moving vehicle. Any person 
appearing remotely must dress and behave pro fessionally in the 
same manner as if physically present in the courtroom. Any 
person appearing remotely must enable their camera when 
joining the proceeding and keep the camera turned on until 
instructed otherwise by the court. Any person appearing 
remotel y must mute their microphone when joining the 
proceeding and keep the microphone turned off until instructed 
otherwise by the court.  
▪ If a witness appears remotely, the party calling the witness 
must ensure the witness has a functioning camera and 
microphone and has tested the internet connection before the 
hearing. The oath will be administered in accordance with 
Florida Rule of General  Practice and Judicial Administration 
2.530.  
D. Submission of Motions and proposed Orders  
• Method of submission : Please refer to the following (3) documents for 
information related to submitting proposed Orders to Florida Courts 
E-Filing Portal. Information can also be found on the 10th Judicial 
Circuit website.  
▪ Administrative Order No. 1 -61.1 
▪ 10th Judicial  Circuit's  Instructions  for submitting  Proposed  
Orders  to Florida's  E-Filing  Portal  
▪ Quick parts & ePortal/ICMS Proposed Orders  
• Order(s) that are not properly formatted will be automatically rejected 
by the Court . 
• All motions must state opposing counsel’s objection or lack of 
objection.  
• All proposed orders must be accompanied by a cover letter either (1) 
certifying that all parties agree to the order or (2) containing a 
Page 5 of 11 statement identifying any disagreement of the parties as to the 
proposed order.  
• Deadline for Submission : Proposed orders must be submitted no later 
than ten (10) days after any hearing unless otherwise directed by the 
Court.  
E. Memorandums and Courtesy Copies of Case Law  
• When required : The Court may require  a memorandum for sentencing 
after trial, open pleas to the Court, and upon formal request of the 
Court. Counsel may send courtesy copies of Case Law or 
Memorandums of Law on any matter counsel finds appropriate.  
• Format : Courtesy copies must be submitted in PDF  format.  
• Submission Method : Memorandums and Courtesy Copies of Case Law 
must be submitted via e -mail to the Judicial Assistant at 
mbrooks@Jud10.FLCourts.org . 
• Deadline for Submission : Memorandums and Courtesy Copies must be 
submitted to the court no later than three (3) days before the matter 
will be heard.  
F. Emergency and other Urgent Matters  
• Requirements : If a party believes there is a factual basis for setting an 
emergency hearing, a detailed motion setting forth the following must 
be filed: (1) the issues to be resolved, (2) reasons why an emergency 
hearing is necessary, and (3) the amount of time neede d for each party’s 
presentation.   If the Court does not act upon an emergency motion 
which requires immediate action, the party  shall present the matter to 
the duty judge.  
• Scheduling : If the court determines that an emergency exists, a hearing 
will be scheduled unilaterally by the court. All parties shall make 
themselves available for the emergency hearing, barring exigent 
circumstances.  
G. Mandatory Docketing  
• Appearances : All parties must appear in -person for Mandatory 
Docketing. Lead trial counsel SHALL be present at Mandatory 
Docketing . Counsel may not waive the Defendant’s presence for 
Mandatory Docketing.  
Page 6 of 11 H. Early Termination of Probation  
• Pro Se Defendants : Defendants who wish to seek a modification 
and/or terminate their probation must submit the request in writing to 
the Felony Clerk’s office at: P.O. Box 9000, Drawer CC -9, Bartow, FL. 
33831 -9000, for processing. The Clerk will notify the Court of the 
pendi ng matter for review. Be advised, processing of the request can 
take up to thirty ( 30) business days.  
• Defendants Represented by Counsel : Counsel shall file the Motion for 
Modification and/or Termination with the Probation Officer’s 
Recommendation Report . See Exhibit C for the Probation Officer form.  
• Ruling:  The Court may rule in Chambers or require a hearing on the 
Motion for Modification and/or Termination.  
I. Other Division Procedures  
• ADA Accommodations : Please contact the Office of the Court 
Administrator, 255 N. Broadway Avenue, Bartow, Florida 33830, 863 -
534-4686, at least 7 days before your scheduled court appearance, or 
immediately upon receiving your court date  notification if the time 
before the scheduled appearance is less than 7 days; if you are hearing 
or voice impaired, call 711.  You can also submit a request online at this 
link: Florida Supreme Court ADA Title II Accommodation Request Form 
| 10th Judicial Circuit Court . 
• Interpreter Requests : If an interpreter is needed for a hearing or trial, 
please review the following link: Court Interpreters | 10th Judicial 
Circuit Court . You can contact the interpreter’s  office via telephone at 
863-534-7700 or via e -mail at CourtInterpreters@jud10.flcourts.org .

COUNTY COURT CIVIL
The County Civil division has jurisdiction over most landlord-tenant disputes, as well as civil matters in which the value of property, debt or other issue of controversy is between $8,001 and $50,000. These cases typically include personal injury protection and other insurance disputes; condominium and homeowner association disputes; repossession and replevin actions; and small claims cases. The County Civil Division has judges assigned at courthouses throughout Broward County, including the West Tower in downtown Fort Lauderdale, as well as regional locations in Deerfield Beach, Hollywood, and Plantation.
Video of Judge Jennifer Hilal Discussing County Civil Eviction Cases
Small claims cases involve cases over property or unpaid bills with a value up to $8,000 (excluding court costs, interest and/or attorney’s fees, if applicable). Small claims lawsuits may be filed by individuals or businesses. Special rules of procedure (
Small Claims Rules)
are designed to make the court process simpler, speedier and more informal than the regular civil court process. For info on small claims court
Click Here
.
Judge Kathleen McCarthy Discusses Small Claims
COUNTY COURT CRIMINAL DIVISION
The County Court Criminal Division handles criminal misdemeanor cases, criminal traffic matters, municipal and county ordinance violations and civil traffic infractions. Criminal misdemeanor cases include violations of the law such as Petit Theft, Simple Battery and Trespassing. Criminal Traffic matters include violations such as Driving While License Suspended, Driving under the Influence and no Valid Driver’s License cases.
Misdemeanor and Criminal Traffic matters are heard by county court judges. First degree misdemeanors are punishable by imprisonment of up to a year in the county jail and a fine of up to $1,000.00. Second degree misdemeanors are punishable by imprisonment of up to 60 days in the county jail and a fine of up to $500.00. Driving under the Influence has its own penalty provisions, which are mandated by law.
Civil Traffic infractions, which are non-criminal related violations, are generally heard by Civil Traffic Hearing Officers and consist of moving and non-moving violations. Moving violations, such as speeding and running a red light, may result in an assessment of points on your license. Other non-moving violations, such as expired registration or no seat belt, do not result in points assessed against your license.
Judge Kenneth A. Gottlieb and Judge Deborah Carpenter-Toye Discussing County Court Criminal Division
The County Court Criminal Judiciary and their staff are located at the Broward County Central Courthouse, 201 SE. 6th Street, Ft. Lauderdale, Fla. 33301 and at the three satellite courthouses located in Hollywood, Plantation

 Judicial Practices and Procedures  
Division P: Juvenile Delinquency, Juvenile Dependen cy, Guardianship, Probate & Mental Health  
(last modified October 8, 2026 ) 
 
Honorable John D. Galluzzo, Circuit Judge 
Stephanie McNeal, Judicial Assistant 
 
Contact Information  
Mailing Address: 190 Eslinger Way, Sanford, FL 32773 
Telephone: 407 -665-5398   
E-mail: Stephanie.McNeal@flcourts18.org  
 
Table of Contents  
A. Communications  with the Judicial  Office  ................................................................................ 1  
B. Scheduling  Procedures  .................................................................................................................. 2  
C. Remote Appearance  ........................................................................................................................ 3  
D. Submission  of Orders  ..................................................................................................................... 3  
E. Courtesy Copies of Case Law & Hearing Materials  .............................................................. 3  
F. Emergency / Urgent Matters  ....................................................................................................... 4  
G. Exhibits for Evidentiary Hearings  .............................................................................................. 4  
H. Motions for Reconsideration  ........................................................................................................ 4  
I. Motions in Limine  ........................................................................................................................... 5  
J. Delinquency  ...................................................................................................................................... 5  
K. Probate  ................................................................................................................................................ 5  
L. Adoptions  ........................................................................................................................................... 6  
M. Guardianship .................................................................................................................................... 6  
N. Incapacity  .......................................................................................................................................... 6  
O. Other  Division  Procedures  ............................................................................................................ 7  
 
A. Communications with the Judicial  Office  
 
• Method of Communication:  All communications to the judicial office 
must be submitted by e -mail to stephanie.mcneal@flcourts18.org . The 
subject line must contain the case number, case name, and relevant 
matter (e.g., 2025-XX-001234-A– In Re: Doe v. Doe). 
 
• Ex parte Communications:  All communications with the judicial office 
must comply with Canon 3 of the Code of Judicial Conduct, which 
2 
 prohibits a judge from initiating, permitting, or considering ex parte  
communications and from considering other communications outside the 
presence of the parties concerning a pending or impending proceeding, 
unless authorized by law. All parties must be copied on any e -mail directed 
to the judicial office, unless an ex parte  communication is authorized by 
law.  
 
• Unsolicited Communications:  Unsolicited communications from non -
parties will not be considered by the court. Parties may only contact the 
judicial office in accordance with these practices and procedures. 
 
• E-Filing Portal Contact Information:  All attorneys and self -represented 
litigants must provide an e -mail address to receive signed orders 
electronically, unless excused. Fla. R. Gen. Prac. & Jud. Admin. 2.516. It 
is the responsibility of attorneys and self -represented litigants to update 
their contact information using Form 2.603 any time there is a change in 
the e-mail account registered for electronic service.  
 
• Response to Inquiries : The Judicial A ssistant is not authorized to provide 
legal advice. If the JA is out of the office, an email will be provided for 
emergencies only.  
 
B. Scheduling  Procedures  
• Scheduling Hearings:  All parties are required to give a good faith 
assessment of the time needed for a hearing . Please contact the JA to 
obtain available dates and times for hearing 
(stephanie.mcneal@flcourts18.org ). Once the hearing has been 
coordinated with all appropriate parties, email the JA to confirm the date, 
time and Courtroom. 
• Notice of Hearing:  A notice of hearing must be filed and served 
immediately after reserving hearing time. Please email a courtesy copy of 
your Notice to the JA. All notices of hearing must contain the ADA 
notification required by Florida Rule of General Practice and Judicial 
Administration 2.540.  If you are setting an evidentiary hearing it must be 
noticed as such. 
• Cancelling Hearings:  You must contact the JA to cancel a hearing. You 
must also file and serve a notice of cancellation on opposing counsel and 
any self-represented litigant and email a copy to the JA. 
• Courtroom:  Judge Galluzzo holds delinquency hearings in Courtroom 1 
and dependency hearings in Courtroom 2 at the Juvenile Justice Center, 
3 
 190 Eslinger Way, Sanford, FL 32771.  For probate, guardianship and 
mental health hearings please contact the JA to determine which 
Courtroom will be used. 
C. Remote Appearance  
 
• Remote Appearance Procedure:  Requests to use communication 
technology for an appearance must be made by motion.  Your proposed 
Order should contain all names and email addresses of the persons 
appearing virtually.  If any virtual attendee will be giving testimony, they 
shall have with them a notary public to swear them in.  
 
• Platform Used: The C ourt uses Microsoft TEAMS  for remote appearances.  
 
• Platform Meeting ID: Contact the JA to obtain the platform meeting ID#  
or TEAMS link.  
D. Submission of Orders  
 
• Format:  All proposed orders must be submitted in  Word Format . All 
proposed orders must be accompanied by a cover letter either (1) 
certifying that all parties agree to the order or (2) containing a statement 
identifying any disagreement of the parties as to the proposed order. 
 
• Submission Method:  Please submit all proposed orders through the  
Florida e-portal. If your proposed order pertains to a matter set for 
hearing before the Court do not submit your order until after the hearing 
has concluded. 
E. Courtesy Copies of Case Law & Hearing 
Materials 
 
• Format : Paper or digital. 
 
• Submission Method : Case law or hearing materials may be hand delivered  
or sent via U.S. mail to 190 Eslinger Way, Sanford, FL 32773. 
 
• Deadline for Submissions : Courtesy copies must be delivered to the Court 
no later than 10 business days before an evidentiary hearing. 
4 
 F. Emergency / Urgent Matters  
 
• Requirements:  If a party believes there is a factual basis for setting an 
emergency hearing, a detailed motion setting forth the following  must be 
filed: (1) the issues to be resolved, (2) reasons why an emergency hearing 
is necessary, and (3) the amount of time needed for each party’s 
presentation.  A courtesy copy of your Emergency Motion must be emailed 
to the JA upon filing. 
 
• Scheduling:  If the Court determines that an emergency exists, a hearing 
will be scheduled unilaterally by the Court.  All parties shall make 
themselves available for the emergency hearing, barring exigent 
circumstances. 
G. Exhibits for Evidentiary Hearings  
 
• Submission Method : Submit all exhibits  in person to the Clerk of Court  
immediately prior to the start of hearing /trial for marking. 
 
• Format:  Exhibits must be submitted in paper format. All attorneys and 
self-represented litigants must bring sufficient copies of each exhibit for 
the clerk, the Court, and each party to review during the hearing or trial.  
Exhibits must be labeled in the following format: “ Petitioner/Plaintiff A for 
identification ” or “Respondent/Defendant A for identification ,” unless 
stipulated then “Exhibit 1.” 
 
• For Remote Hearings:  Submit exhibits in person via hand delivery; via 
electronic mail; or via U.S. mail to the Judicial Assistant at least 7 days 
prior to the scheduled hearing. Please contact the Judicial Assistant via 
email to coordinate receipt if via hand delivery.  The Judicial Assistant will 
provide the exhibit(s) to the Clerk of Court on the day of hearing / trial. 
H. Motions for Reconsideration  
 
• Submission Method : Upon  filing of your Motion for Reconsideration 
please email a courtesy copy to the JA for the Court’s review. 
 
• Scheduling : If after review the Court determines that a hearing is 
necessary the JA will contact the parties to coordinate. 
5 
 I. Motions in Limine  
 
• Scheduling : All Motions in Limine and Pre Trial Motions must be 
submitted and set for hearing prior to the trial date. Please contact the JA 
for available hearing dates/times. 
J. Delinquency  
 
• Arraignment:  Attorney and juvenile appearances may be waived  with a 
properly filed Notice of Appearance, Entry of Plea and Waiver of 
Arraignment. 
 
• Docket Sounding : All parties (juvenile, parent/guardian, and attorney) 
must be present in -person at docket sounding.  For Docket Sounding, if 
there is not a pre -filed Motion to Continue, the parties with their attorney 
may appear at Docket Sounding and address their continuance request 
with the State Attorney and, assuming no objection, the Clerk will issue a 
new Docket Sounding date and the parties may leave prior to court 
beginning, however, the juvenile and parent/guardian must wait to sign 
for their minutes.  It is encouraged to file your Motion to Continue in 
advance of Docket Sounding to alleviate the need for attorney, juvenile and 
parent/guardian to appear.  **Please note in your Motion to Continue 
that your client is waiving speedy trial. ** Attorneys, of course, are 
always welcome to address detention status, GPS and home detention 
issues at Arraignment and/or Docket Sounding should they wish to wait 
for Court to begin. 
K. Probate  
 
• Uncontested:  The Court does not require hearings on any uncontested 
probate matters nor a checklist prior to submitting orders.  Please file your 
Petition(s) and submit your proposed Order(s) via the e -portal. To avoid 
unnecessary rejections of Orders, please ensure that a death  certificate, 
waivers/consents (if applicable), affidavit of heirs (if applicable), funeral 
receipt showing proof of payment (if necessary), original will (if applicable), 
and any other pertinent documents are filed and docketed by the Clerk.  
Additionally , all homestead petitions and Orders must include the 
property address, a legal description and the Parcel ID number.   
 
• Trials:  Once you have noticed the case for trial, you must contact the JA 
to schedule a Case Management Conference before the Court to determine 
scheduling, witness/exhibit exchange, discovery cutoff, etc. 
6 
 L. Adoptions  
 
• Hearings : Please contact the JA for available dates and times to schedule 
the adoption hearing. 
 
• Notice of Hearing : Notices  of Hearing MUST be filed in both the 
Dependency and Adoption  case(s).  Please also email a courtesy copy of 
your Notice of Hearing to the JA .  Please review the Uniform Chapter 39 
Adoption Checklist attached hereto. 
M.  Guardianship  
 
• Appointment of Emergency Temporary Guardians : Petitions  for 
Appointment of an Emergency Temporary Guardian do not require a 
hearing.  Please submit your proposed Order and Letters once the Petition 
has been accepted and docketed by the Clerk. 
 
• Approval of Minor Settlements  and Appointment of Guardian : For  
settlements exceeding net proceeds of $15,000.00 or more, please submit 
an Order Appointing a Guardian ad Litem.  Once the GAL’s report has 
been filed, and all credit reports and background checks have been filed, 
you may submit your proposed Order approving settlement and appointing 
guardian. If a hearing is necessary, the Court will contact you to schedule 
same. 
N. Incapacity  
 
• Appointment of Attorney/Elisor : After  you have filed your Petition to 
Determine Incapacity and it has been accepted and docketed by the Clerk, 
please submit an Order Appointing Attorney/Elisor. The Clerk of Court 
will assign the Attorney/Elisor based on rotation and indigency status. 
 
• Appointment of Examining Committee : Please  contact one of the 
physicians below to confirm their acceptance of appointment.  Once 
confirmed, please submit an Order Appointing Examining Committee with 
the physician’s contact information contained therein.  The Clerk of Court 
will assign the remaining members based upon rotation. 
 
1. Karl G. Sieg, M.D.  - 5415 Lake Howell Road, #110 , Winter Park, FL 
32792 - (407) 718-9053 - kgsieg@yahoo.com  18th Circuit 
2. Daniel Kan, M.D. - 4670 Babcock St. Palm Bay, FL 32905 - (321) 
241-4693 - Dkan2160@gmail.com   18th Circuit 
7 
 3. Melanie Melendez Garcia, M.D.  - 13920 Landstar Blvd., #45 
Orlando, FL 32824 - (863) 800 -5323 - 
melendezmd@mgmedicalcenter.com   9th Circuit – Alternative 
4. Nasreen Razack -Malik, M.D. - 6167 Harbor Town Ct. Orlando, FL 
32819 - (321) 304 -2422 - nasreenorlando@yahoo.com   9th Circuit - 
Alternative 
5. Earl P. Taitt, M.D. - 4151 Hunters Park Ln., #100 Orlando, FL 32837 
- (407) 856-8830 - office@taittmd.com   9th Circuit - Alternative 
 
 
• Hearing : Once  all examining committee reports have been filed, please 
contact the JA to schedule a hearing to determine incapacity. You must 
submit an Order Compensating Exam Committee prior to setting the 
incapacity hearing .  Orders compensating the Exam Committee shall 
state the amount payable to each member; that the members shall be paid 
either (1) by the State of Florida (indigent); or (2) from the assets of the 
Ward (not indigent), and that payment shall be made within 10 days of the 
date of the Order to avoid the issuance of an  Order to Show Cause and/or 
Contempt.  
O. Other  Division  Procedures  
 
• ADA Accommodations: If you are a person with a disability 
who needs any accommodation in order to participate  in a 
proceeding, you are entitled, at no cost to you, to  the 
provision of certain assistance. Please contact the  ADA 
Coordinator, Court Administration, 301 North Park A venue, 
Sanford, FL  32771, telephone number (407) 665 -4227 at 
least 7 days before your scheduled court appearance , if you 
are hearing or voice impaired, call 711.  
 
• Interpreter Requests: If an interpreter is needed for a hearing or trial, 
please contact Court Administration . SEMINOLE INTERPRETER 
REQUEST (SOLICITUD DE INTÉRPRETE PARA SEMINOLE)   
interpreter.seminole@flcourts18.org .  
 
8 
 UNIFORM CHAPTER 39 ADOPTION CHECKLIST  
 
The following documents are required to be attached to, or filed along with, the petition for adoption 
pursuant to section 39.812 and Chapter 63, Fla. Stat. : 
 
____ A copy of the consent executed by the department, unless waived pursua nt to § 63.062(7). See § 
39.812(5), Fla. Stat .  
 
____ A statement, signed by the prospective adoptive parents, acknowle dging receipt of all information 
required to be disclosed under § 63.085(2). See § 39.812(6), Fla. Stat.  
 
____ A form provided by the department, which details the social and me dical history of the child and 
each parent and includes the social security number and date of birth for each parent , if such information 
is available or readily obtainable. See § 39.812(6), Fla. Stat. 
 
____ A certified copy of the court judgment terminating parental ri ghts under chapter 39. See § 
63.112(2)(a), Fla. Stat.  
 
____ Favorable Preliminary Home Study. A preliminary home study must be c onducted before placing 
the minor in the intended adoptive home. § 63.092(3), Fla. Stat. The home study must be conducted within 
1 year of child custody pursuant to § 63.092(3) and § 63.112(2)(b), Fla. Stat. 
 
____ A copy of any declaratory statement previously entered by the court pu rsuant to sections 63.102. and 
63.112(2)(c), Fla. Stat.  
 
____ Certificate of the results of the Florida Putative Father Registry se arch provided in section 
63.054(7)(b),  Fla. Stat.  See also § 63.037, Fla. Stat.  This document is ONLY required if a search was not 
previously completed or a search was previously com pleted but documentation of the search is not 
contained in the case file.  
 
If child is 12 years of age or older:  
 
_____Documentation that an interview was held with the minor, if older than 12 years of age, unless the 
court, in the best interest of the minor, dispenses with the minor's consen t under § 63.062(1)(c)  and § 
63.112(2)(d), Fla. Stat.  
 
____ Final Home Investigation. The final home investigation must be conducted before the adoption 
becomes final. The investigation may be conducted by a licensed c hild-placing agency or a professional 
in the same manner as provided in § 63.092, Fla. Stat . to ascertain whether the adoptive home is a suita ble 
home for the minor and whether the proposed adoption is in the best int erest of the minor. See § 63.125(2), 
Fla. Stat. . _____Consent executed by child 12 years of age or older (unless Court dispenses with consent in the best 
interest of minor).  See 63.062(1)(c), Fla. Stat .

COUNTY COURT CIVIL
The County Civil division has jurisdiction over most landlord-tenant disputes, as well as civil matters in which the value of property, debt or other issue of controversy is between $8,001 and $50,000. These cases typically include personal injury protection and other insurance disputes; condominium and homeowner association disputes; repossession and replevin actions; and small claims cases. The County Civil Division has judges assigned at courthouses throughout Broward County, including the West Tower in downtown Fort Lauderdale, as well as regional locations in Deerfield Beach, Hollywood, and Plantation.
Video of Judge Jennifer Hilal Discussing County Civil Eviction Cases
Small claims cases involve cases over property or unpaid bills with a value up to $8,000 (excluding court costs, interest and/or attorney’s fees, if applicable). Small claims lawsuits may be filed by individuals or businesses. Special rules of procedure (
Small Claims Rules)
are designed to make the court process simpler, speedier and more informal than the regular civil court process. For info on small claims court
Click Here
.
Judge Kathleen McCarthy Discusses Small Claims
COUNTY COURT CRIMINAL DIVISION
The County Court Criminal Division handles criminal misdemeanor cases, criminal traffic matters, municipal and county ordinance violations and civil traffic infractions. Criminal misdemeanor cases include violations of the law such as Petit Theft, Simple Battery and Trespassing. Criminal Traffic matters include violations such as Driving While License Suspended, Driving under the Influence and no Valid Driver’s License cases.
Misdemeanor and Criminal Traffic matters are heard by county court judges. First degree misdemeanors are punishable by imprisonment of up to a year in the county jail and a fine of up to $1,000.00. Second degree misdemeanors are punishable by imprisonment of up to 60 days in the county jail and a fine of up to $500.00. Driving under the Influence has its own penalty provisions, which are mandated by law.
Civil Traffic infractions, which are non-criminal related violations, are generally heard by Civil Traffic Hearing Officers and consist of moving and non-moving violations. Moving violations, such as speeding and running a red light, may result in an assessment of points on your license. Other non-moving violations, such as expired registration or no seat belt, do not result in points assessed against your license.
Judge Kenneth A. Gottlieb and Judge Deborah Carpenter-Toye Discussing County Court Criminal Division
The County Court Criminal Judiciary and their staff are located at the Broward County Central Courthouse, 201 SE. 6th Street, Ft. Lauderdale, Fla. 33301 and at the three satellite courthouses located in Hollywood, Plantation

Judges

Judges

The First Judicial Circuit includes Escambia, Santa Rosa, Okaloosa, and Walton Counties. Twenty-six circuit judges and twelve county judges serve within the Circuit and are assisted by general magistrates and hearing officers in hearing and disposing of cases. Judges are elected by the voters of the Circuit in non-partisan elections and serve for six-year terms.

Circuit judges handle all circuit court cases, including felony criminal, domestic relations (family), probate, guardianship, juvenile (both dependency and delinquency), and civil suits in which more than $50,000 is at issue.

County court judges handle county court cases, including misdemeanor criminal, landlord-tenant, small claims, traffic, and civil suits in which $50,000 or less is at issue.

Under the Florida Code of Judicial Conduct, judges cannot speak to parties or members of the public regarding pending cases. Judges are permitted to consider arguments made only during court proceedings and in documents filed by parties in a case.

JUDGE JONATHAN A. SKINNER  
COUNTY COURT CRIMINAL DIVISION 7 
Courtroom 3F  
18th Judicial Circuit  
 
All counsel shall be familiar with and are expected to abide by the Rules 
Regulating the Florida Bar and the Guidelines for Professional Conduct.  
Moreover, all parties shall be familiar with and follow all Administrative Orders 
of the Florida Supreme Court and the 18th Judicial Circuit. This Court is held to 
the additional standards set forth in the Code of Judicial Conduct and the 
Principles of Professionalism for Judges.   
Location: Moore Justice Center, Courtroom 3F, 2825 Judge Fran Jamieson 
Way, Viera, Florida 32940  
Judicial Assistant: Email is the most effective way to communicate with the 
Court. Please note that it is never appropriate to include legal argument or 
substantive discussion regarding facts in any case in emails to a Judicial 
Assistant. Always include both parties in email communications with the 
Judicial Assistant.  
Eva Walls: Phone (321) 617-7256 Email: eva.walls@flcourts18.org   
 
Docket Sounding  
Privately represented Defendants are excused from Private Docket Sounding if 
the defense attorney excused their client.  
Inmates will not be transported for Docket Sounding unless specifically 
requested by the Defense Attorney.  
Virtual appearances on TEAMS can be considered when a party is ill, out of state, 
or unable to travel. Approval to appear Virtual must be granted prior to the 
hearing.  
Please note that parties present in the courtroom will be addressed prior to the 
court addressing those parties appearing via TEAMS.  
Public Defender Docket Sounding  
The Public Defender may waive the client’s appearance if they have had good 
contact with their client. The Public Defender may request a virtual appearance 
for any client who is ill, located out of state, or unable to travel. Approval to 
appear virtually must be granted prior to the hearing. 
Defendants represented by the Office of the Public Defender should contact 
their attorney’s office at (321) 617-7373 with any questions they may have 
regarding their appearance at Docket Sounding.  
All Violation of Probation, Non-Jury Trial, Infraction Hearings, Order to 
Show Cause, Motion Hearings:  
Attendance is required in person unless previously excused by the Court.  Transportation of Inmates. Please email the Judicial Assistant and BCSO 
Court Deputy David Wilson (david.wilson@bcso.us) to confirm the inmate is 
scheduled for transport. 
 
VIRTUAL/TEAMS/SPECIAL EXCEPTIONS:  Parties may request a special exception for TEAMS/remote appearances by E-
Filing a Motion with the Clerk of Court and copying the Judicial Assistant at 
least 48 hours prior to the Court event.  
Motions:  
Motions must be E- filed, copied to the opposing side for objection/input, and 
scheduling.  
If no objection, the attorneys shall email the motion to the Judicial Assistant, 
copying the opposing party and including the language of no objection. The 
parties will prepare an appropriate Order and forward it to the Judicial Assistant 
for signature.  
Motions and orders are not to be submitted through E-Portal. All motions and 
orders should be emailed to the Judicial Assistant directly. Please include all 
case style information when emailing the Judicial Assistant (Case Number, Defendant’s Name, etc.)  
Hearing times/JACS:  
As hearing times are often set quickly, Judge Skinner does not use JACS for 
coordinating and scheduling hearings. Please contact Judicial Assistant, Eva 
Walls at: eva.walls@flcourts18.org for assistance.  
Continuances must be requested in writing. 
Pleas  
Plea hearings are encouraged to proceed as set. The Court will accept open pleas 
to the Court at any time.  
Pleas in Absentia will be accepted in all cases. Plea in Absenti a paperwork must 
be submitted to Judge Skinner’s Judicial Assistant prior to the scheduled court 
date. Counsel may appear by phone or TEAMS link, or they may opt to waive 
their appearance completely. The plea form must be notarized.  The fingerprint 
card must be done by a law enforcement agency with an ORI number on the 
fingerprint card. 
Violation of Probation Arraignments and Hearings  
Pro Se Defendants must appear in-person in court unless excused by the Court.   
Early Resolution Hearings  
Felony ER Arraignment and Public Defender ER are addressed at: 8:00 a.m.  
Private Counsel ER cases are addressed at 8:30 a.m.  
If requesting a conti nuance, contact the ER State Attorney, and if no objection, 
the ER State Attorney will provide a new ER court date, and this date is required 
to be included on any proposed Continuance Order submit ted to the Judicial 
Assistant for signature. 
Pro Se Defendants must be present for ER Arraignments and Early Resolution 
Hearings.  
Calendar Call 
Attendance is required by all parties in-person unless previously excused 
by the Court.  
Jury Trial  
Judge Skinner will conduct a Calendar Call on the first day of the trial week. All 
attorneys and Defendants must appear in person for the Calendar Call. Pro Se 
Defendants must appear in court. Any inmates on the docket will be transported 
Mental Health Court  Mental Health Court is scheduled once  a month. Defendants should keep in 
contact with the assigned Circles of Care representative throughout the Mental 
Health Court process. All Defendants should appear on the assigned court date before Judge Skinner. Requests to appear virtually may be submitted via email 
to the Judicial Assistant and will be reviewed by the Judge on a case-by-case basis by the Judge.  
Any questions regarding policy and procedure for Division 7/Judge Jonathan A. 
Skinner in Courtroom 3F, please contact the Judicial Assistant: Eva Walls at 
eva.walls@flcourts18.org. 
 
REMOTE HEARING/COURTROOM DECORUM AND BEHAVIOR  
1. All parties and counsel shall exercise proper courtroom decorum, including 
dressing in appropriate courthouse attire, while in the Court in person or by 
remote appearance. See Administrative Order 09-06 for more details.  
2. All parties and counsel shall address all remarks to the Court, not opposing 
counsel or the opposing party.  3. Maintain composure and proper tone of voice throughout the proceedings. 
Attorneys should not raise their voice toward the court, counsel, witnesses, or 
jurors.  
4. Avoid disparaging personal remarks or acrimony toward opposing counsel and 
remain wholly detached from any ill feeling between the litigants or witnesses.  5. Refer to all persons, including witnesses, other counsel, and the parties by 
their surnames and not by their first or given names unless the permission of 
the Court is sought in advance.  
6. Only one attorney for each party shall examine or cross-examine each witness. 
The attorney stating objections, if any, during direct examination shall be the 
attorney recognized for cross-examination.  
7. In making objections, counsel should state only the legal grounds for the 
objection and shall withhold all further comments or arguments unless 
elaboration is requested by the Court. If elaboration is requested, each party will 
have the opportunity to provide an argument. The party making the objection 
shall provide the argument first, then the opposing party will have the 
opportunity to respond, and the court will rule.  
8. When referencing case law to court and counsel, attorneys are required to 
provide the full citation of the case for court and counsel.  9. All parties and counsel shall refrain from gestures, facial expressions, audible 
comments, or the like, as manifestations of approval or disapproval during the 
testimony of witnesses, or at any other time.  
10. All parties, counsel, and witnesses must be stationary when appearing. The 
person appearing may NOT be driving a vehicle. The person appearing must be in a location that is quiet, private, and without distractions. 
If you are a person with a disability who needs any 
accommodation in order to participate in this proceeding, you 
are entitled, at no cost to you, to the provision of certain 
assistance. Please contact the ADA Coordinator, Moore Justice 
Center, 2825 Judge Fran Jamieson Way, 3rd Floor, Viera, FL, 
32940, 321- 633-2171, ext. 3, at least 7 days before your 
scheduled court appearance, or immediately on receiving this 
notification if the time before the scheduled appearance is less 
than 7 days; if you are hearing or voice impaired, call 711.

Judge Ramsey’s Division Procedures
Alachua Family DR2, 1/5 DV, and Bradford Circuit Family
(Updated 04/27/2026)
AI IN THE COURTS
If any attorney for a party, or a pro se party, has used Artificial Intelligence (“AI”) in the preparation of any complaint, answer, motion, brief, or other paper filed with the Court, and assigned to Judge Ramsey, MUST, in a clear and plain factual statement disclose that AI has been used in any way in the filing, and CERTIFY, that each and every citation to the law or the record in the paper has been verified as accurate.
Communications with the Judicial Office
Method of Communication:
All communications to the judicial office must be submitted by e-mail to
ThomasC@circuit8.org
. The subject line must contain the case number including the county code, case name, and relevant matter (e.g., 01-2024-CF-001234-A: State v. Doe – 2-Hour Hearing Requested).
Ex parte Communications:
Please note that the Code of Judicial Conduct governing behavior by judges forbids the judges of the Eighth Judicial Circuit to discuss pending cases with the public. Please do not call or email the Court expecting to speak with a Judge about any case. If you have a comment to make, please mail it to the Clerk’s Office. Please keep in mind that the Court is only allowed to consider arguments made in court and documents filed by actual parties to the case. They cannot ethically read or consider any other opinions or arguments about the case, and they cannot give legal advice. Thank you.
Unsolicited Communications:
Unsolicited communications from non-parties will not be considered by the Court. Parties may only contact the judicial office in accordance with these practices and procedures.
E-Filing Portal Contact Information:
All attorneys and self-represented litigants must provide an e-mail address to receive signed orders electronically, unless excused. Fla. R. Gen. Prac. & Jud. Admin. 2.516. It is the responsibility of attorneys and self-represented litigants to update their contact information using
Form 2.603
any time there is a change in the e-mail account registered for electronic service.
E-Filing Website
Scheduling Procedures
Court Schedule:
Master Calendar – Alachua Circuit Civil, Family, and Juvenile
Master Calendar – Bradford Circuit Court
Hearing Requests:
You must use the
hearing request form
to email all hearing requests to
ThomasC@circuit8.org
. Hearing requests are not accepted by telephone.
Please confirm that your motion has been filed, served on all parties, and docketed prior to requesting hearing time. No hearing time will be given for motions that are not filed and docketed. If you have questions about whether your motion is filed and docketed, please contact the
Alachua County Clerk of Court
. When a motion is e-filed the Judge does not always receive a copy. If you file a motion that the Judge needs to see or act upon, you must provide a copy to the Judicial Assistant,
ThomasC@circuit8.org
. All proposed orders must be submitted through the E-Portal.
The notice of hearing shall include the full title of the motion and filing date, the length of the hearing, and shall advise if the hearing will be conducted in person or via Zoom.
Once confirmation of the hearing date has been received by email from the judicial assistant, a notice of hearing shall be prepared by the moving party.
If all parties may not receive notice of a hearing in sufficient time for the timeframe requested below, the Court may extend the timeframe for a matter to be heard. The Court will attempt to accommodate all requested timeframes but can make no assurance of availability on the Court’s calendar.
Hearing Availability:
It is
mandatory
that all parties consult with one another regarding their availability for hearing. If a hearing is unilaterally set without any effort to coordinate a date and time with opposing counsel, that matter will not be heard by the Court. However, if a party has made a good faith attempt to schedule a hearing with opposing counsel and counsel has failed to respond after
three (3)
attempts via email and/or phone, then the party may schedule the hearing unilaterally. Any hearings scheduled unilaterally pursuant to these instructions
must
include a note on the Notice of Hearing stating
“Set Unilaterally Pursuant to Judge Van Vorst’s Divisional Instructions.”
Further, counsel attending any hearing unilaterally set pursuant to these instructions will be expected to present proof of attempts to coordinate with opposing counsel at the hearing.
Hearing Time:
The moving party is responsible for requesting the appropriate amount of hearing time. Parties should presume that each side will be given an equal amount of time. If motions from multiple parties are set during the same hearing time, each moving party is responsible for requesting the appropriate amount of time.
If there is a concern that a hearing may exceed the allotted time, either party may request for the Court to allot an equal amount of time to each party at the beginning of the hearing, or the Court may distribute time sua sponte. Parties will be responsible for presenting the entirety of their argument and presentation of evidence within their allotted time.
Continuance Procedure:
You must contact opposing counsel to determine if they have an objection prior to filing a Motion for Continuance. The Motion must be filed with the Clerk of Court and must indicate if opposing counsel objects to the continuance. If the continuance is agreed to by all parties, please submit an Agreed Order to the appropriate e-portal for the case’s division. If the opposing party objects to the continuance, it may be necessary to set a hearing on the Motion but still upload a proposed order to the appropriate e-portal for the case’s division.  Please see the procedure for scheduling a hearing. The Court will evaluate the Motions for Continuance on a case-by-case basis even if the opposing party agrees or does not object to the continuance.
Cancelling Hearings:
No hearing shall be cancelled unless the parties have the written agreement from the Court. Please notify the Court at least 24 hours in advance of any requests to cancel.
Motions for Re-hearing/Reconsideration:
Upon filing said motion, email a copy Court for review. The Court will either rule without a hearing or will advise the moving attorney to schedule a hearing. While an email may suffice in the correction of scrivener’s errors, please remember that emails pointing out errors do not toll the time for rehearing or reconsideration under the Rules.
ID Requirement:
If a party or witness will provide testimony at the scheduled hearing, the Court must receive by email to
ThomasC@circuit8.org
, a photograph copy of their driver’s license or photo ID no later than three (3) business days prior to the hearing.
Remote Appearance
Motions for appearance by Zoom will be considered by the Court on a case-by-case basis.  A request for Zoom appearance may be denied.  If your client will appear in-person in court, a Zoom appearance by counsel will be denied.  In order to file a motion for Zoom appearance, you must have a fully operational camera.  Use of your camera is required for Zoom appearances.
Please be advised that if your case is set on a block docket (such as pretrial conferences) and you are attending by Zoom, your case will be called after all other cases with in-person appearances are called.
ALL MOTIONS FOR ZOOM APPEARANCE MUST BE FILED IN THE COURT FILE AT LEAST 3 BUSINESS DAYS PRIOR TO THE SCHEDULED COURT DATE.  A PROPOSED ORDER GRANTING THE ZOOM APPEARANCE MUST BE UPLOADED TO THE CASE’S DIVISION PORTAL AT LEAST 3 BUSINESS DAYS PRIOR TO THE SCHEDULED COURT DATE. FAILURE TO TIMELY FILE THE MOTION AND UPLOAD THE CORRECT ORDER TO THE EPORTAL, WILL RESULT IN DENIAL OF THE MOTION. THE COURT WILL PROVIDE THE ZOOM INFORMATION UPON APPROVAL OF THE COURT.
Submission of Orders and Judgments
Format for Proposed Orders:
All proposed orders shall include the following coding after the body of the proposed order.  This coding allows our computer system to input the proper dates and signatures for processing.
DONE AND ORDERED
in Chambers at Gainesville, Alachua County, Florida on DDDD.
JJJJ
CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE
I HEREBY CERTIFY
that copies have been furnished by U.S. Mail or via filing with the Florida Courts E-Filing Portal on MMMM.
CCCC
AAAA
Should an additional party or address be required for service of the order that is not contained in the court file, please type the name of the party who is to receive the order, as well as that party’s e-mail/e-service address OR mailing address at the end of the AAAA block in the Certificate of Service.
Submission Method:
Proposed orders shall be submitted via the Florida Courts E-Filing Portal (
www. https://www.myflcourtaccess.com/
). Do not send proposed orders by United States Mail or email unless the proposed order is in PDF format. Please see the instructions above for formatting.
If there are parties who have not consented to use of e-mail service, stamped envelopes should be mailed or hand delivered to the Judicial Assistant, Candace Thomas. Please clip the envelopes together, along with a sticky note that indicates the case name and case number. PLEASE DO NOT ADDRESS THE ENVELOPES; LEAVE THE ENVELOPES BLANK BUT BE SURE TO ADD THE PROPER POSTAGE.
Orders will not be entered until the motion has been docketed and imaged by the Clerk. Docketing and imaging by the Clerk may take more than 48 hours from electronic filing.
Courtesy Copies of Case Law and Other Documents
Cases being relied upon by the parties at a hearing or trial should be provided to opposing counsel and the Court no later than three (3) business days prior to the hearing. However, the Court will always consider any law applicable to the matters being litigated. Litigants should highlight the parts of a law or case that they believe are pertinent to the issues at hand. All other non-exhibit documents that a party wishes the Court to review must be provided to the Court and the opposing party by email to
ThomasC@circuit8.org
at least three (3) business days prior to the hearing or trial. Each case or document should be provided as a separate file.
Please confer with all parties prior to the hearing to determine whether there are any stipulations as to the admissibility of evidence. Any pre-marked evidence which is stipulated should be so noted. All other pre-marked evidence will be considered to be opposed.
Emergency and Other Urgent Matters
Emergency Motions:
A copy of any “Emergency” motion e-filed with the Clerk of Court and served upon opposing counsel should be provided to the Judge’s office for review by emailing
ThomasC@circuit8.org
.  If a hearing is requested, please follow the directions for Hearing Requests. If the Court determines that a hearing should be granted, the Court will advise the moving party of an expedited date and time for the hearing.
A party requesting emergency action must include the words “Emergency Motion” in the title of the motion and must set forth in detail the nature of the emergency, the date by which a ruling is necessary, and the reason the ruling is needed by the stated date. The emergency motion process should only be used in situations where a child is threatened with harm or where a party plans to improperly remove a child from the state. See
Loudermilk v. Loudermilk
, 693 So. 2d 666 (Fla. 2d DCA 1997). If one of these circumstances exists or another that rises to the level that would require immediate action to prevent harm, a party may file an emergency motion. The unwarranted designation of a motion as an emergency motion may result in sanctions.
All emergency motions must be verified. Emergency motions must be e-mailed to the judicial assistant for the Court’s review. If the motion fails to raise an actual emergency, it will be denied to the extent that it seeks emergency relief (but not as to the merits) and may be scheduled to be heard in the ordinary course.
A party whose time-sensitive motion does not qualify as an emergency motion but who nonetheless requires an expedited ruling by a date certain may file an expedited motion. An expedited motion must include the words “Expedited Motion” in the title and must set forth in detail the date by which an expedited ruling is needed and the reason the ruling is needed by the stated date. As a general matter, an expedited motion is one that will become moot if not ruled upon by a date certain.
Parties are reminded that difficulties with timesharing or other problems that are not objectively extremely serious and imminent are NOT emergencies.
Exhibits for Evidentiary Proceedings
If you intend to present any evidence or documents to the court at your hearing, you must pre-mark all items for identification (ex. “Petitioner’s Exhibit A, B, C..”) and serve a copy via Certified US Mail to all parties no less than ten (10) business days prior to the hearing.
Digital Exhibits that cannot be sent via US Mail (i.e., videos, flash drives, etc.) must be included on the exhibit list (and properly marked) and hand delivered directly to the opposing counsel or party no later than ten (10) business days prior to the hearing.
In addition, a
paper copy
of all pre-marked exhibits, along with an Index of Exhibits from each side, shall be received by the Court via Certified US Mail or by hand delivery to the Court’s Gainesville office no later than the deadline contained in your specific order, or five (5) business days prior to the hearing date. This packet will be used by the Court to stamp the official evidence as it is entered at the hearing/trial.
The Court will not accept electronic devices (i.e., videos, flash drives, etc.) sent via US Mail; you may submit a physical copy at hearing/trial.
Please confer with all parties prior to the hearing to determine whether there are any stipulations as to the admissibility of evidence. Any pre-marked evidence which is stipulated, should be so noted. All other pre-marked evidence will be considered opposed.
Evidence should not be filed with the Clerk.
Pretrial Procedures and Conferences
All requests to set hearings must be emailed pursuant to the scheduling procedures above. Please be advised that filing a motion to set hearing must be emailed to the judicial assistant,
ThomasC@circuit8.org
, and a hearing must be requested pursuant to the scheduling procedures.
Setting Case for Trial or Final Hearing
All requests to set trial or final hearing must be emailed pursuant to the scheduling procedures above. Please be advised that filing a motion to set trial or final hearing must be emailed to the judicial assistant,
ThomasC@circuit8.org
, and a hearing must be requested pursuant to the scheduling procedures.
Notices of Appearance, Motion to Withdraw and Substitution of Counsel
Pursuant to Florida Rules Procedure, all motions to withdraw or for substitution of counsel must contain the client’s signature/consent and specific reason(s) for the withdraw/substitution. Additionally, all proposed orders granting withdrawal shall be accompanied by the filing of an email designation form for the client or notice to the Court that an email designation has been previously filed. If an attorney is unable to obtain client consent or an email designation filled out by the client, then the motion to withdraw or to substitute counsel may be set for hearing. Motions to withdraw filed after the case has been set for trial may not be granted, and all such orders shall include notice to the now pro se litigant of the date and time of the previously scheduled hearing or trial. Motions to withdraw, even with consent, may require a hearing if filed prior to an already scheduled hearing or trial.
MOTIONS TO WITHDRAW AS THE ATTORNEY OF RECORD:
When filing a Motion to Withdraw as Attorney of Record, you are required to include the client’s contact information, including address and e-mail address if any, within the text of the Motion and any proposed order on same. You are also required to serve on your client a copy of the Motion to Withdraw and a Notice of Hearing. You must include your client’s name and contact information in the certificate of service for both the Motion to Withdraw and the Notice of Hearing.
Your proposed order must include your client’s contact information and indicate that your client has 30 days to retain new counsel and have counsel file a notice of appearance or your client shall be deemed to be proceeding pro-se unless the party must be represented per the rules of civil procedure.
If you have your client’s written consent to withdraw there is no need to set your Motion to Withdraw for hearing. Instead, please file a consent to withdraw signed by the client in the court file.  Please submit your proposed order with the client’s contact information to the e-portal for the case division.
SUBSTITUTION OF COUNSEL:
Stipulations for substitution of counsel between law firms shall be signed by both the former attorney, the new attorney taking over the case and must include written client consent. The Stipulation shall be filed in the court file.  A proposed order may be submitted through the e-portal for the case division.  The Court will not grant a substitution of counsel unless client’s written consent is obtained.

Jonathan Schlechter

Jonathan Schlechter
SCHEDULE A HEARING
County: Walton County
Type: Circuit
Divisions: C
Phone: (850) 892-8472
Fax: N/A
Judicial Assistant: Tracie Fields, Tracie.Fields@Flcourts1.Gov
Address: Walton County Courthouse, 571 U.S. Highway 90 East DeFuniak Springs, FL 32433

A. Communications with the Judicial Office

Method of Communication: All communications to the judicial office must be submitted by e-mail to Tracie.fields@flcourts1.gov. The subject line of any e-mail to the judicial office must contain the case number, case name, and relevant matter (e.g., 2024 DR 001234 SC – Doe v. Doe – 2-Hour Hearing Requested).
Ex parte Communications: All communications with the judicial office must comply with Canon 3 of the Code of Judicial Conduct, which prohibits a judge from initiating, permitting, or considering ex parte communications and from considering other communications outside the presence of the parties concerning a pending or impending proceeding, unless authorized by law. All parties must be copied on any e-mail directed to the judicial office, unless an ex parte communication is authorized by law.
The Judge’s Assistant is unable to provide legal advice, interpret court rules, explain how to file documents, or advise parties on legal rights or on what actions to take in your case. Questions regarding legal matters should be directed to a licensed attorney or other appropriate legal resources.
The Florida Courts electronic portal can be found at the following link: Florida Courts E-Filing Portal | File Court Documents Online
The above website contains a frequently asked questions section and a how to section.
Unsolicited Communications: Parties may only contact the judicial office in accordance with these practices and procedures. Unsolicited communications from non-parties will not be considered by the court.
E-Filing Portal Contact Information: All attorneys and self-represented litigants must make and receive service by e-mail, which is generally through the Florida Courts E-Filing Portal, unless excused. Fla. R. Gen. Prac. & Jud. Admin. 2.516.

B. Scheduling Procedures

Any motion(s) must be filed and docketed before submitting a request for hearing time.
Final hearings/Trials must be scheduled by email to the JA at Tracie.Fields@flcourts1.gov.
Temporary Relief Hearings will generally be scheduled for 1 hour. Temporary relief hearings should be scheduled via OnceHub. If no hearing time is available on OnceHub within 45 days please contact Judge Schlechter’s JA to schedule the Temporary Relief Hearing. Judge Schlechter makes every effort to schedule Temporary Relief Hearings within 45 days of the hearing request.
All other hearings 90 minutes or less must be scheduled via OnceHub.
Hearings for more than 90 minutes must be scheduled directly with Judge Schlechter’s office by emailing his JA at tracie.fields@flcourts1.gov
Notice of Hearing: Notice of Hearing must be filed and served immediately after reserving hearing time.

If the hearing is scheduled to occur via Zoom, the notice must contain the Court’s Zoom ID.

All notices of hearing must contain the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) notification required by Florida Rule of General Practice and Judicial Administration 2.540.

Submission Deadlines: The Court requires parties to comply with the Courtesy copy procedures outlined below.
Continuance Procedure: Requests to continue must be in writing and filed with the Clerk.
Cancelling Hearings: To cancel a hearing, the Court’s judicial assistant must be immediately notified via e-mail and a notice of cancellation must be filed.
Cancelling Final Hearings: Final Hearings may only be cancelled by court order. Any such request must be in writing and filed with the clerk and a courtesy copy emailed to the Court’s Judicial Assistant.

C. Remote Appearance

Remote Appearance Procedure: Generally, any hearing scheduled for 1 hour or less may be conducted via Zoom if all parties agree. If all parties do not agree, an in-person hearing will be required and a motion and proposed order to appear by Zoom will be required.
All Final Hearings/Trials will be in person. If a party seeks to have anyone appear via Zoom a motion and proposed order to appear by Zoom will be required.
Platform Used: Zoom (Zoom link will be provided after the hearing date is confirmed.)
Requirements: Participants must be able to use the audio and video functions of zoom. If the hearing is an evidentiary hearing, failure to have working video may result in the exclusion of testimony.

D. Submission of Orders and Judgments

Format: Word.
Submission Method: E-portal unless directed otherwise by the Court.
Deadline for Submissions: 10 days unless directed otherwise by the Court.
Other Procedures Relating to Submission of Orders and Judgments: Proposed orders on contested motions should only be submitted if directed to do so by the Court.

E. Courtesy Copies of Case Law and Other Documents

When Required: All contested hearings (all case types).
Format: PDF. Do not submit hard copies/binders.
Submission Method: E-mail to the Court’s judicial assistant.
Deadline for Submissions: 7 days prior to the hearing.
Procedures: All documents should be combined into one (1) PDF. The PDF should be named in the following format: Case Number Party’s name Motion Name DIN of Motion, i.e. 2025CA000001 Smith Motion for Summary Judgment DIN 35.The PDF must be searchable, contain a table of contents, and bookmarks for each item. The documents in the PDF should be in the following order:
Table of Contents
Notice of Hearing
Motion/Opposition/etc.
Opposing Party’s Motion/Opposition (if the party desires)
Reply (if applicable)
Supporting documents
Case law
Other items

Instructions to add bookmarks to a PDF can be found on the Adobe website as well as many other websites.

Each party should only submit 1 PDF.

F. Emergency and Other Urgent Matters

Requirements: As required by law.
Scheduling: If the Court determines that an emergency exists, a hearing will be scheduled unilaterally by the Court. The parties must make themselves available for the hearing.

G. Exhibits for Evidentiary Proceedings

Submission Method: For remote proceedings, all evidence must be filed electronically with the Clerk of Court at least 3 business days prior to the hearing.

For in person proceedings, the Court prefers that exhibits be electronically filed at least 3 business days prior to the hearings. If the exhibits have been filed with the Clerk 3 days prior to the hearing, paper or electronic exhibits may be used to question witnesses. If exhibits have not been filed with the Clerk at least 3 business days prior to the hearing, paper exhibits must be used. Exhibits should be marked prior to the hearing.

H. Pretrial Procedures and Conferences

Case Management Conference: May be requested by any party or scheduled unilaterally by the Court.
[Other Procedures Relating to Pretrial Procedures and Conferences]: A trial order will be entered that establishes all relevant deadlines.

I. Setting Case for Trial

Procedure: For family law cases, request a final hearing via email with Judge Schlechter’s JA. The hearing will be scheduled and an Order Setting Trial/Final Hearing will be prepared by the Court. A Case Management Conference may be required for any final hearing requesting more than 1 day.

J. Forms

The Florida State Court System maintains a self-help center. The self-help center provides general information for self-represented litigants and access to numerous family law specific forms. The self-help center can be accessed by clicking on the following link:

Family Law Forms / Domestic Relations Court Resources / Family Courts / Services - - Florida Courts

Usage:
[Other Forms Procedures]:

K. Other Division Procedures

ADA Accommodations: Please contact Court administration at Phone (850) 595-4400 Fax (850) 595-0360, ADA.Walton@flcourts1.gov at least 7 days before your scheduled court appearance, or immediately upon receiving this notification if the time before the scheduled appearance is less than 7 days; if you are hearing or voice impaired, call 711.
Procedures for Motions to Withdraw/Substitution Of Counsel: In accordance with Florida Rule of General Practice and Judicial Administration 2.505, written consent of the client must be filed with the Clerk of Court and opposing counsel (if any) must have no objection to the withdrawal/substitution. If the client has not signed consent and/or opposing counsel has an objection to the withdrawal, a hearing is required.

Checking the Status of Orders: To inquire about the status of an order, please check the clerk's website first:

Walton County Clerk of Courts & Comptroller

ALL ORDERS SHALL CONTAIN THE FOLLOWING LANGUAGE ABOVE THE JUDGE’S SIGNATURE BLOCK:

DONE AND ORDERED in Chambers, DeFuniak Springs, Walton County, Florida.

CROSS-SETTING OR “PIGGY-BACKING” HEARINGS: When a hearing is initially scheduled, the time set aside for the original motion is deemed to be sufficient for that matter only. Adding additional motions is not possible unless there are no objections by opposing counsel/parties to doing so and adequate additional time is available.

About Us

The First Judicial Circuit is one of 20 judicial circuits in Florida. Our courts serve the people of Escambia, Okaloosa, Santa Rosa, and Walton Counties.

Judges

The First Judicial Circuit includes Escambia, Santa Rosa, Okaloosa, and Walton Counties. Twenty-six circuit judges and twelve county judges serve within the Circuit and are assisted by general magistrates and hearing officers in hearing and disposing of cases. Judges are elected by the voters of the Circuit in non-partisan elections and serve for six-year terms.

Circuit judges handle all circuit court cases, including felony criminal, domestic relations (family), probate, guardianship, juvenile (both dependency and delinquency), and civil suits in which more than $50,000 is at issue.

County court judges handle county court cases, including misdemeanor criminal, landlord-tenant, small claims, traffic, and civil suits in which $50,000 or less is at issue.

Under the Florida Code of Judicial Conduct, judges cannot speak to parties or members of the public regarding pending cases. Judges are permitted to consider arguments made only during court proceedings and in documents filed by parties in a case.

Judges

The First Judicial Circuit includes Escambia, Santa Rosa, Okaloosa, and Walton Counties. Twenty-six circuit judges and twelve county judges serve within the Circuit and are assisted by general magistrates and hearing officers in hearing and disposing of cases. Judges are elected by the voters of the Circuit in non-partisan elections and serve for six-year terms.

Circuit judges handle all circuit court cases, including felony criminal, domestic relations (family), probate, guardianship, juvenile (both dependency and delinquency), and civil suits in which more than $50,000 is at issue.

County court judges handle county court cases, including misdemeanor criminal, landlord-tenant, small claims, traffic, and civil suits in which $50,000 or less is at issue.

Under the Florida Code of Judicial Conduct, judges cannot speak to parties or members of the public regarding pending cases. Judges are permitted to consider arguments made only during court proceedings and in documents filed by parties in a case.
